[Section: On the Breach of the Covenant by the Banu al-Nadir]

Then the Banu al-Nadir broke the covenant. Al-Bukhari said: this took place six months after Badr, as related by 'Urwa. The cause of this was that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out to them with a group of his Companions, and spoke to them asking that they assist him with the blood-money (diyya) for the two men of the Banu Kilab whom 'Amr ibn Umayya al-Damri had killed. They said: "We will do so, O Abu al-Qasim. Sit here until we fulfil your need." Then they withdrew to confer among themselves, and Satan made the wretchedness that had been decreed for them seem attractive to them, so they conspired to kill him (ﷺ). They said: "Which of you will take this millstone, climb up, and drop it on his head to crush him with it?" Their most wretched man, 'Amr ibn Jahhash, said: "I will." Salam ibn Mishkam said to them: "Do not do it, for by God he will be informed of what you have planned, and it is a breach of the covenant between us and him." Immediately, revelation came to him from his Lord, blessed and exalted, concerning what they had intended. He rose swiftly and headed for Madina, and his Companions caught up with him and said: "You rose before we noticed you." So he informed them of what the Jews had plotted. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to them: "Leave the city, and do not live with me in it. I have given you a term of ten days; whoever I find here after that, I will strike his neck." They remained for some days preparing for departure. The hypocrite 'Abd Allah ibn Ubayy sent to them: "Do not leave your homes, for I have two thousand men who will enter your fortress with you, and they will die before you do; Quraiza and your allies from Ghatafan will also support you." Their leader Huyayy ibn Akhtab was tempted by what he had been told, and he sent to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) saying: "We will not leave our homes, so do what you wish." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions said takbir and rose against them, with 'Ali ibn Abi Talib carrying the banner. When he reached them, they stood on their fortresses shooting arrows and hurling stones, while Quraiza withdrew from them, and Ibn Ubayy and their allies from Ghatafan betrayed them. For this reason, God, glorified and exalted, likened their story and made their example: ﴿Like the example of Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you."﴾ [al-Hashr: 16].

Indeed, Surat al-Hashr is the surah of the Banu al-Nadir, and in it is the beginning of their story and its end.

So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) besieged them, cut down their palm trees, and burned them. They sent to him: "We will leave the city." He granted them that they should leave with their lives and their families, and that they could take whatever their camels could carry, except weapons. The Prophet (ﷺ) took possession of the property and the weaponry (al-halaqa), which is arms. The Banu al-Nadir were exclusively for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), for his needs and the interests of the Muslims, and he did not take a fifth (khums) of it because God granted it to him as spoils (fay'), and the Muslims did not charge against it with horses or riding camels. He did take a fifth from Quraiza.

Malik said: the Messenger of God (ﷺ) took a fifth from Quraiza, but did not take a fifth from the Banu al-Nadir, because the Muslims did not charge against the Banu al-Nadir with their horses or camels, as they did against Quraiza. He expelled them to Khaybar, and among them was Huyayy ibn Akhtab, their chief. He seized the weapons, and took control of their land, homes and property. He found fifty coats of mail, fifty helmets, and three hundred and forty swords. He said: "These, among their people, are in the position of the Banu al-Mughira among Quraysh." Their story took place in Rabi' al-Awwal in the fourth year after the Hijra.

**(Chapter)**

Ibn al-Qayyim said, after some discussion:

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought refuge from poverty and linked it with disbelief, saying: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty."

Good is of two kinds: the good of the Hereafter, whose opposite is disbelief, and the good of this world, whose opposite is poverty. Poverty is the cause of the punishment of this world, and disbelief is the cause of the punishment of the Hereafter. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made giving zakat (obligatory alms) the duty of the wealthy and receiving it the duty of the poor. He distinguished between the two hands, the giving hand and the receiving hand, both in the Law (shar') and in decree (qadar). He made the hand of the giver higher than the hand of the receiver, and He made zakat the impurities of wealth. For this reason He forbade it to His best creation and to his family, as a protection for them, an honouring of them, and an elevation of their status.

We do not deny that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was poor and that Allah then enriched him. Allah opened [the means] to him, bestowed [wealth] upon him, and made him prosperous. He would store for his household a year's provision, and he would give gifts such as no one else gave. He gave as one who does not fear poverty, and he died leaving [the revenues of] Fadak and al-Nadir, and wealth that Allah had specifically given him.

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾.

Thus his Lord, glorified is He, exempted him from the poverty that would make charity lawful for him, and He compensated him for what He had exempted him from with the most noble, lawful and excellent wealth. That is what he took by the shade of his spear and the edge of his sword from the enemies of Allah, who held Allah's wealth unjustly and aggressively. Allah had created wealth to be used in obeying Him, and it was in the hands of disbelievers and wicked people, unjustly and aggressively. So when it returned to His allies and the people of His obedience, what He had created for them was restored to them. But the wealth and sovereignty of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were not of the same kind as the wealth and possessions of the people of this world. Their wealth is in possessing things, and his wealth was in being free of need for things, which is the lofty richness. Their sovereignty is one in which they dispose of things according to their desires, whereas he disposed of his property only as a servant disposes of it, acting only on the command of his master.

The jurists have disagreed over whether fay' was the property of the Prophet (ﷺ), with two opinions, both of which are reports from Ahmad.

The verified position is that his ownership was of a different kind, namely ownership in which he disposes of the property by command, as he said: "By Allah, I do not give to anyone, nor do I withhold from anyone; I am only a distributor, placing it where I am commanded." This is from the perfection of the rank of his servanthood. For this reason, he left no inheritance, for he was a pure servant in every respect to his Lord, mighty and majestic. A servant has no property to be inherited from him. Thus Allah, glorified is He, combined for him the highest kinds of richness and the most noble kinds of poverty. His ranks of perfection were complete, so neither of the two groups had more right to him than the other.

In his poverty he was the most patient and most thankful of Allah's creatures, and likewise in his richness. Allah, the Exalted, made him an exemplar for both the rich and the poor.

What greater richness is there than that of one to whom the keys of the treasures of the earth were offered, and to whom it was proposed that Safa be turned to gold? He was given the choice between being a king-prophet and being a servant-prophet, and he chose to be a servant-prophet. Despite this, the wealth of the Arabian Peninsula and Yemen was brought to him, and he spent all of it, keeping nothing for himself. Instead he took on the dependents and the debts of the Muslims, and he said: "Whoever leaves wealth, it is for his heirs; and whoever leaves a burden (kall, i.e. dependants or debts), it is for me and upon me."

So Allah, glorified is He, elevated his status above being among the poor to whom zakat is lawful, just as He exempted him from being among the rich who are made wealthy by inherited property. Rather, He made him free of need through Himself, enriched his heart with complete richness, and extended to him the utmost abundance. He spent to the utmost, gave the finest gifts, and did not hoard wealth. He did not acquire property, land or estates. He left no sheep, camel, slave, female slave, dinar or dirham.

**[Section: On his ruling concerning the division of wealth]**

The wealth that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to distribute was of three kinds: zakat, spoils of war (ghana'im), and fay'.

As for zakat and spoils of war, their rulings have already been mentioned, and we explained that he did not distribute them among all eight categories, and that sometimes he placed them in only one category.

As for his ruling on fay', it is established in the authentic collections that on the day of Hunayn he distributed some of the fay' among those whose hearts were to be reconciled (al-mu'allafa qulubuhum), and he gave the Ansar nothing. They complained about this, so he said to them: "Are you not content that people should go away with sheep and camels, while you go away with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), leading him to your homes? By Allah, what you return with is better than what they return with." The story and its benefits have already been mentioned in its proper place.

The point here is that Allah, glorified is He, permitted His Messenger, in the ruling regarding fay' property, what He did not permit to anyone else.

In the authentic collection, from him (ﷺ): "I give to some people and leave others, yet the one I leave is dearer to me than the one I give to."

Also in the authentic collection, from him: "I give to some people, fearing their impatience and their distress, and I entrust others to the richness and goodness that Allah has placed in their hearts; among them is Amr ibn Taghlib." Amr ibn Taghlib said: "I would not love to have, in exchange for the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), red camels."

In the authentic collection: "Ali was sent to him from Yemen with a gold ingot, and he divided it into four parts. He gave to al-Aqra' ibn Habis, to Zayd al-Khayl, to Alqama ibn Ulatha, and to Uyayna ibn Hisn. A man with sunken eyes, a protruding forehead, a thick beard and a shaven head stood up before him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, fear Allah!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Woe to you! Am I not the most deserving of the people of the earth to fear Allah?'" The hadith continues.

In the Sunan: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) assigned the share of the near kin (dhawi al-qurba) to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, and he left out the Banu Nawfal and the Banu Abd Shams. Jubayr ibn Mut'im and Uthman ibn Affan went to him and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not deny the virtue of the Banu Hashim because of their position with you; but what of our brothers, the Banu al-Muttalib, whom you gave to while you left us out, when we and they are on the same level?' The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'We and the Banu al-Muttalib do not separate in the Jahiliyya or in Islam; we and they are one thing,' and he interlaced his fingers."

Some people have mentioned that this ruling is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ), and that after him the share of the near kin is to be spent on the Banu Abd Shams and the Banu Nawfal just as it is spent on the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib. They said: "Because Abd Shams, Hashim, al-Muttalib and Nawfal are brothers, and they are the sons of Abd Manaf." It is also said that Abd Shams and Hashim were twins.

The correct view is that this prophetic ruling continues, and that the share of the near kin belongs to the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib, since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) specified it for them. The claim that this is specific to the Prophet (ﷺ) is false. He explained the places of the khums which Allah assigned to the near kin, so these places may not be exceeded and may not be fallen short of. However, he did not divide it among them equally between their rich and their poor, nor did he divide it according to the rule of inheritance, where the male receives the portion of two females. Rather, he spent it on them according to benefit and need: he married off their unmarried, paid the debts of their debtors, and gave their poor enough for their sufficiency.

In the Sunan of Abu Dawud, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entrusted me with the fifth of the fifth (khums al-khums), and I placed it where it belonged during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), during the lifetime of Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and during the lifetime of Umar, may Allah be pleased with him."

This has been used as evidence that it was spent on its five categories. This argument is not strong, for at most it shows that he spent it on the categories on which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to spend it, and he did not extend it beyond them. Where then is the generalization of the five categories from it? What the guidance and rulings of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicate is that he made the categories of the khums the same as the categories of zakat, and he did not go beyond the categories mentioned. He did not distribute it among them as an inheritance division. Whoever carefully considers his biography and guidance will have no doubt about this.

In the two Sahihs, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The wealth of the Banu al-Nadir was among what Allah restored to His Messenger, which the Muslims had not obtained with horses or camels. It was therefore exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from which he spent on his family a year's provision." In another wording: "He would set aside for his family the provision of their year, and what remained he would put into horses and weapons as preparation in the way of Allah."

In the Sunan, from Awf ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When fay' came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he would distribute it on the same day, giving the one with a family two shares and giving the single person one share."

This is a preference from him for those with families, according to benefit and need, even if his wife was not among the near kin.

The jurists have disagreed about fay', whether it was the property of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to dispose of as he wished, or whether it was not his property. There are two opinions in the school of Ahmad and others.

What his Sunnah and guidance indicate is that he disposed of it by command: he placed it where Allah commanded, and he distributed it to those to whom he was commanded to distribute it. He did not dispose of it as an owner disposes of property according to his desire and will, giving to whom he loved and withholding from whom he loved. Rather he disposed of it as a commanded servant disposes of property, carrying out what his master and lord commanded him, giving to whom he was commanded to give and withholding from whom he was commanded to withhold.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stated this explicitly, saying: "By Allah, I do not give to anyone, nor do I withhold from anyone; I am only a distributor, placing it where I am commanded."

His giving, withholding and distributing were thus by mere command. Allah, glorified is He, gave him the choice between being a servant-messenger and being a king-messenger, and he chose to be a servant-messenger.

The difference between the two is that a servant-messenger disposes of nothing except by the command of his master and sender, whereas a king-messenger may give to whom he wills and withhold from whom he wills. This is as Allah, the Exalted, said to the king-messenger Solomon: ﴿This is Our gift, so bestow or withhold without account﴾ [Sad: 39]. That is: give to whom you wish and withhold from whom you wish; We will not call you to account. This is the rank that was offered to our Prophet (ﷺ), but he turned away from it to what was higher, namely the rank of pure servanthood, in which the one who has it disposes of matters only by the command of his master in every detail, great and small.

The point is that his disposal of fay' was of this kind. He was a king who differed from the ruling of other owners. For this reason he would spend from what Allah had restored to him, of what the Muslims had not obtained with horses or camels, on himself and his family for a year's provision, and he would place the remainder in horses and weapons as preparation in the way of Allah, mighty and majestic. This kind of wealth is the share over which disputes have arisen to this day.

As for zakat, spoils of war and the division of inheritance, these are specifically assigned to their recipients, and no one else shares in them. Therefore, what became unclear for the rulers after him regarding fay' did not become unclear regarding these, and no dispute arose over them as it did over fay'. Had the nature of his property not become unclear to them, Fatima, the daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would not have sought her inheritance from his estate, thinking that what was his property would be inherited from him as with other owners. The true nature of the ownership that is not inherited from him was hidden from her, may Allah be pleased with her. Rather, it is charity after him. When his successor, the rightly guided, righteous Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and those rightly guided caliphs after him knew this, they did not make what he left of fay' an inheritance to be divided among his heirs. Rather, they handed it to Ali and al-Abbas to manage as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had managed it. Then they disputed over it and brought their case to Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Umar, and neither of them divided it as inheritance, nor did they grant it to al-Abbas and Ali. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger, and to the near kin, the orphans, the needy and the wayfarer, so that it does not become a circulating [wealth] among the rich among you. Take what the Messenger gives you, and abstain from what he forbids you, and fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment. [It is] for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from Allah and approval, and supporting Allah and His Messenger; those are the truthful. And [it is for] those who were settled in the abode and in faith before them, who love those who emigrate to them﴾ [al-Hashr: 7–9], up to His saying: ﴿And those who came after them﴾ [al-Hashr: 10], through the end of the verse [al-Hashr: 7–10].

Allah, glorified is He, has informed us that what He restored to His Messenger, in its entirety, belongs to those mentioned in these verses. He did not single out its khums for those mentioned. Rather, He made it general, unrestricted and comprehensive. It is spent first on the specific categories, who are the people of the khums, and then on the general categories, who are the emigrants, the helpers, and their followers until the Day of Judgment.

Therefore, those who acted upon it, namely he and his rightly-guided successors (al-Khulafa' al-Rashidun), are the intended meaning of these verses. This is why ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) said, in what Ahmad (may Allah have mercy on him) and others narrated from him: "No one has a greater right to this wealth than anyone else, and I have no greater right to it than anyone else. By Allah, there is no Muslim but that he has a share in this wealth, except a enslaved servant. Rather, we are at our ranks in the Book of Allah, and our shares from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). A man has his trial (bala') in Islam, a man has his precedence (qidam) in Islam, a man has his usefulness (ghina') in Islam, and a man has his need. By Allah, if I remain alive for them, the shepherd at Mount San'a will certainly reach his share of this wealth while he is still tending his place."

So those mentioned in the verse of the fay' (spoils/revenue) are the same as those mentioned in the verse of the khums (one-fifth). The Muhajirun, the Ansar and their followers are not included in the verse of the khums, because they are the rightful recipients of the whole fay'. The people of the khums have two entitlements: a specific entitlement from the khums and a general entitlement from the whole fay'. They are included in both shares.

Just as the division of the whole fay' among those designated for it is not a division of property among co-owners, such as the division of inheritances, bequests and absolute property, but is according to need, benefit, usefulness in Islam and trial therein, so too is the division of the khums among its people. Their origin is one in the Book of Allah. The explicit mention of the five categories establishes their inclusion, and that they never fall outside the people of the fay' in any circumstance, and that the khums does not pass beyond them to others, just as the categories of zakat do not pass beyond them to others. Likewise, the general fay' in the verse of al-Hashr belongs to those mentioned in it and does not extend beyond them to others.

For this reason, the leading imams of Islam, such as Malik, Imam Ahmad and others, ruled that the Rafidah (Rafidites) have no right to the fay', because they are neither among the Muhajirun, nor the Ansar, nor among those who came after them, saying: ﴿Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith﴾. This is the view of the people of Madinah, the preference of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, and it is what the Qur'an indicates, as well as the practice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his rightly-guided successors.

People have differed concerning the verse of zakat and the verse of the khums. Al-Shafi'i said: the division of zakat and khums must be made among all the categories, and one gives from each category to whoever is called by the name of the plural.

Malik (may Allah have mercy on him) and the people of Madinah said: rather, one gives within the categories mentioned in both, and does not extend beyond them to others. The division of zakat and fay' is not obligatory among all of them.

Imam Ahmad and Abu Hanifa said: they agree with Malik (may Allah have mercy on them both) regarding the verse of zakat, and with al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) regarding the verse of the khums.

Whoever reflects upon the texts and the practice of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his successors will find that it indicates the view of the people of Madinah. Allah, glorified is He, made the people of the khums the people of the fay', and specified them out of concern for their affair and to give them precedence. Since the spoils of war (ghanaʾim) belong specifically to their own people, with no one else sharing in them, He explicitly stated the khums of them for the people of the khums. Since the fay' is not restricted to one person over another, He made its whole for them, for the Muhajirun, the Ansar and their followers. Thus He equalized the khums and the fay' in their disbursement. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would spend the share of Allah and his own share on the interests of Islam, and four-fifths of the khums on its people, giving priority to the most important and the most in need. He would marry off their unmarried men from it, pay their debts from it, help those among them in need, give a single share to the unmarried and two shares to the married. Neither he nor any of his successors would gather the orphans, the needy, the wayfarers and the near relatives, and divide the four-fifths of the fay' among them equally or by preference. Likewise, they did not do this with zakat. This is his guidance and his way, and it is the decisive word and the pure truth.
