Ibn al-Qayyim, after some discussion, said:

This al-Zubayr and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf are superior to most of the Companions, despite their abundant wealth, and their influence on the religion is greater than the influence of the People of the Suffah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade wasting wealth, and informed that leaving one's heirs wealthy is better than leaving them in poverty. He also informed that the owner of wealth who spends seeking the face of Allah will only increase in rank and elevation by it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sought refuge from poverty and linked it with disbelief, saying: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from disbelief and poverty." The good is of two kinds: the good of the Hereafter, whose opposite is disbelief, and the good of this world, whose opposite is poverty. Poverty is thus a cause of the punishment of this world, and disbelief is a cause of the punishment of the Hereafter. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, made giving zakat the duty of the wealthy and receiving it the duty of the poor, and He distinguished between the two hands legally and in fact, making the hand of the giver higher than the hand of the taker. He made zakat the filth of wealth, and for this reason He forbade it to His best creation and to his family, in protection of them, honouring them and raising their status.

We do not deny that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was poor and then Allah enriched him. Allah granted him victory, gave him provision and expanded upon him. He would store the provision of a year for his family, and would give gifts that no one else was given. He gave with the generosity of one who does not fear poverty. He died leaving Fadak, al-Nadir and wealth which Allah had specifically given him. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah and to the Messenger﴾.

So his Lord, glorified is He, exempted him from the poverty that makes charity lawful, and compensated him for what He had exempted him from with the most noble, lawful and excellent wealth, which is what he took under the shade of his spear and the edge of his sword from the enemies of Allah, whose hands held the wealth of Allah unjustly and aggressively. Indeed, He created wealth to be used in obeying Him, and it was in the hands of disbelievers and wicked people unjustly and aggressively. When it returns to His allies and the people of His obedience, it reverts to them, what He created for them. But the wealth and sovereignty of the Messenger of Allah were not of the same kind as the wealth and possessions of the people of this world. Their wealth is wealth in a thing, and their being free from a thing is the high wealth. Their sovereignty is one in which they dispose of as they wish, whereas he disposed of his property only as a servant who acts solely by the command of his master.

**(Benefit)**

Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, or Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, used to circumambulate the House, and his only supplication was: "My Lord, protect me from the avarice of my soul, my Lord, protect me from the avarice of my soul."

It was said to him: "Will you not supplicate with something other than this?"

He said: "If I am protected from the avarice of my soul, then I have prospered."

The difference between *shuḥḥ* (avarice, a severe greed that drives a person to pursue and hoard a thing) and *bukhl* (miserliness) is that *shuḥḥ* is an intense eagerness for a thing, an insistence in seeking it, an exhaustive effort to obtain it, and a craving of the soul for it. *Bukhl* is withholding the spending of a thing after one has obtained it, loving it and clinging to it. Thus, one is *shaḥīḥ* (avaricious) before obtaining it and *bakhīl* (miserly) after obtaining it.

So miserliness is the fruit of avarice, avarice calls to miserliness, and avarice lies latent in the soul. Whoever is miserly has obeyed his avarice, and whoever is not miserly has disobeyed his avarice and been protected from its evil, and that is the one who prospers: ﴿And whoever is protected from the avarice of his soul, it is those who are the successful﴾.

**[Section: The difference between *al-wajd* (the feeling of being aggrieved) and *al-ḥiqd* (rancour)]**

The difference between *al-wajda* (being aggrieved by someone) and *al-ḥiqd* (rancour) is that *al-wajd* is the sensing of pain, the awareness of it, and the stirring of the soul to remove it, and so it is a perfection. As for *al-ḥiqd*, it is concealing evil and anticipating it at all times toward the one with whom one is aggrieved, so that its effect never departs from the heart.

Another difference: *al-mawjida* (the grievance) is for what has reached you from him, while *al-ḥiqd* is for what he has reached from you. *Al-mawjida* is the existence of the harm that has reached you from his injury, while *al-ḥiqd* is the anticipation of the existence of retaliation from him. *Al-mawjida* is quick to pass, while *al-ḥiqd* is slow to pass. *Al-ḥiqd* comes with the constriction of the heart and the domination of the darkness and smoke of the soul over it, unlike *al-mawjida*, which accompanies its strength, firmness, the power of its light, and its perception.

**(Section)**

Abu al-Abbas ibn al-Arif, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

"It has been said: love is preferring the beloved over others."

This definition is also of the same kind as what preceded it, for preferring the beloved over others is the requirement and consequence of love. When love is settled in the heart, it demands from the lover the preferring of his beloved over others, and this preference is the sign of its establishment and soundness. If he prefers something other than the beloved over him, he is not a lover of him, even if he claims to be. He is only a lover of himself and of his own benefit from the one he loves. When he sees another benefit that is dearer to him than the benefit he seeks from his beloved, he prefers that benefit over the beloved.

This is a point where people often err greatly, since most of them love for their own benefit and aim. When he knows that the one he loves is with another, he loves that other as one loves means to an end, not for his own sake. This appears in two situations:

The first: he sees another benefit for himself with someone else, so he prefers that benefit and abandons his beloved.

The second: when he obtains that benefit from his beloved, his love cools, his heart is calmed, and the settled love departs from his heart, as it has been said: "Whoever loves you for a matter, will turn away once it ends." This is a love mixed with ulterior motives.

Rather, pure love is that one loves the beloved for his perfection, and that he deserves to be loved for his essence and attributes.

What makes this love necessary is the annihilation of the servant from his own will in favour of the desire of his beloved, so that he acts upon his beloved's desire from him, not upon his own desire from his beloved.

This is pure love, free from the filth of ulterior motives and the impurities of the soul, and it necessarily entails preferring the beloved over others. Whenever the authority of this love is stronger, this preference is more complete and increases. Concerning such a matter it has been said:

*You disobey God while claiming to love Him; by your life, this is a monstrous analogy.*
*If your love were true, you would obey Him; the lover is indeed obedient to the one he loves.*

Here is a subtle point that must be grasped: preferring the beloved is of two kinds:

Preferring by exchange and trade, and preferring by love and will.

The first: one prefers his beloved over others seeking his benefit from him, so he gives what he prefers in order to be repaid with something better.

The second: one prefers him in response to the call of love, for true love constantly summons him to prefer his beloved. His preferring is his most noble benefit, so his benefit lies in the act of preference itself, not in the compensation sought by it. Only a refined, pious, illuminated soul understands this, while a coarse soul has no knowledge of it, and it is not its nest, so it does not wriggle.

The whole of religion and dealing rests on preference, for it is giving precedence and singling out the one you prefer with what you prefer for him over yourself. It has even been said that a condition of it is need on the part of the one who prefers, for if he were not in need of it, giving would be generosity and magnanimity.

This applies only to preferring created beings. Allah, glorified is He, prefers His servant over others without any need on His part, for He is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy. In the supplication transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ): "O Allah, increase us and do not diminish us, give us and do not deprive us, honour us and do not humiliate us, prefer us and do not prefer others over us, and be pleased with us and make us pleased."

It has been said: whoever Allah prefers over others, Allah prefers him over others.

The difference between *al-īthār* (preference) and *al-athara* (self-favouring) is that *al-īthār* is singling out another with what you desire for yourself, while *al-athara* is your exclusive possession of it over others.

In a hadith: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took our pledge to hear and obey in our hardship and our ease, in our eagerness and our reluctance, and in self-favouring over us."

Having understood this, preference either relates to created beings or relates to the Creator. If it relates to created beings, its perfection is that you prefer them over yourself with what does not waste your time, does not corrupt your state, does not diminish your religion, does not block your path, and does not withhold your provision.

If preferring them involves any of that, then preferring yourself over them is better, for a man is one who does not prefer anyone over his share from Allah, whoever he may be.

This is extremely difficult for the wayfarer, and the first is easier than it.

For the praiseworthy preference by which Allah praised its doer is preference with worldly things, not with time, religion, or what returns to the soul's well-being. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9].

He informed that their preference is only with the thing which, when a man is protected from avarice regarding it, makes him among the successful. This is only the surplus of worldly goods, not the times devoted to acts of obedience.

Indeed, complete success lies in being stingy with them (the times), for whoever is not stingy with his time will be left by people upon the earth, a bankrupt in plain sight. Being stingy with time is thus the cultivation of the heart and the preservation of its capital.

Among what proves this is that He, glorified is He, commanded competition in righteous deeds, rivalry in them, and hastening toward them, which is the opposite of preferring others with them. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden whose width is the heavens and the earth﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 133]; He said: ﴿So race to the good deeds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 148]; and He said: ﴿And for that let the competitors compete﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 26].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If people knew what there is in the call to prayer and the first row, they would draw lots for it."

Drawing lots occurs only at crowding and competition, not at preference. So the Lawgiver did not make acts of obedience and devotion a place for preference, but a place for competition and racing. For this reason the jurists said: preferring others in acts of devotion is not recommended. The wisdom in this, and Allah knows best, is that preference occurs only with a thing that is too narrow to be shared, so that it cannot accommodate both the preferrer and the preferred, rather only one of them. As for acts of righteousness and obedience, there is no constraint upon the servants in them. If thousands upon thousands shared in one act of obedience, there would be no constraint or crowding upon them, and it would contain them all. Even if crowding is assumed over a single act or place, such that it cannot be performed by all – so that if one performs it, it escapes the others – there is still in the resolve and firm intention to do it the reward that its doer would have, as is established from the Prophet (ﷺ) in more than one hadith. If the actual performance is missed, his resolve and intention to do it are not lost to him.

Moreover, if it escapes him, there is in other acts of obedience and devotion a substitute for it: either equal to it, or greater, or less.

Whenever he performs the substitute, and Allah knows from his intention and his true resolve his desire for that missed deed, Allah gives him its reward and the reward of what he substituted for it, thus combining both for him.

That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.

Moreover, the purpose is the servant's eagerness to draw near to Allah, seeking the means to Him and competing for what He loves. Preferring others in this drawing near indicates one's aversion to it and abandonment of it, and a lack of competition for it. This differs from what the servant needs of his food, drink, and clothing, when his brother is also in need of them: if one of them is singled out with it, the other misses out. So when the servant finds in himself strength and patience to prefer with it, Allah, glorified is He, encourages him to do so, provided it does not break his religion, bring him a corruption, cut off a path he resolved to travel toward his Lord, or disturb his heart such that it makes him attached to created beings. The corruption of preferring this is weightier than its benefit. When the benefit of preferring is greater, such that it includes rescuing another from destruction, ruin, or dire necessity – and the preferrer has no equivalent of it – preferring becomes obligatory for him. If he has its equivalent, preferring is not obligatory for him, but if he does it, it would be the utmost generosity, munificence, and goodness, for whoever prefers another's life over his own and another's necessity over his own has reached the limit of generosity and munificence, exceeded its extent, and taken the fullest share of it.

There are juristic questions connected with this topic, which this is not the place to mention.

If it is asked: what makes this preference easy for the soul, since the soul is created disposed to self-favouring rather than to preference?

It is said: several things make it easy:

The first: the servant's desire for noble character and its highest qualities. Among the best and noblest and highest character traits of a man is preference. Allah has created hearts to honour its possessor and love him, just as He has created them to hate the one who monopolises and to despise him. There is no alteration in the creation of Allah. Character traits are three: the trait of preference, which is the trait of superiority; the trait of distribution and equality, which is the trait of justice; and the trait of monopolising and domineering, which is the trait of injustice.

The possessor of preference is beloved, obeyed, and revered. The possessor of justice is one against whom souls have no way to harm or dominate, yet they do not submit to him as they submit to one who prefers them. The possessor of monopoly: souls hasten to harm him and dominate him more swiftly than a flood rushes down a slope. Did anything but monopoly ever destroy kingdoms and uproot them? For souls have no patience with it. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded his companions to hear and obey the rulers even if they monopolise over them, because of the hardship and aversion in obeying a monopolist.

The second: aversion to the traits of the base, and abhorrence of avarice and hatred of it.

The third: magnifying the rights that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, has made obligatory for Muslims over one another. He observes these rights with due observance, fears neglecting them, and knows that if he does not give beyond what is just, he cannot remain within its limit, for that is very difficult. Rather he must go beyond it to excellence, or fall short of it into injustice. Out of fear of neglecting the right and falling into wrong, he chooses to prefer with what does not diminish or harm him, and thereby gains a beautiful reputation in this world and great reward in the Hereafter, along with the blessing and abundant good that preference brings him, so that what returns to him from his preference is better than what he gave. Whoever has tested this knows it, and whoever has not tested it should examine the conditions of the world. The successful one is the one whom Allah, glorified and exalted is He, grants success.

**(Section)**

Preference relating to the Creator is more sublime and excellent than this. It is preferring His pleasure over the pleasure of others, preferring His love over the love of others, preferring fear of Him and hope in Him over the fear and hope of others, and preferring humility before Him, submission, lowliness, supplication, and seeking favour from Him over displaying these to others. Likewise preferring to ask Him and to lay one's needs before Him over attaching that to anyone else. The first is when one prefers some servants over himself in what is beloved to him; this is preferring Allah over others, and his self is among the greatest of others. So he prefers Allah over it, abandoning its beloved for the beloved of Allah.

The sign of this preference is two things:

The first: doing what Allah loves when the soul dislikes it and flees from it.

The second: abandoning what He dislikes when the soul loves it and desires it. By these two matters the station of preference is sound. The burden of this preference is heavy because of the dominance of other things and the strength of the call of habit and disposition. The trial in it is great, the burden in it is severe, and the soul is weak in regard to it. The servant's success and felicity are not complete except by it, and it is easy for one whom Allah makes it easy for. So it is right for the servant to aspire to it even if the ascent is difficult, and to strive toward it even if its gift is great, and to bear a small risk for a great kingdom and a great triumph. The fruit of this, in the immediate and the deferred, does not resemble the fruit of any other deed. A little of it lifts the servant up, and what he attains by it, others cannot attain over long periods. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills. Love is not realized except through this preference.

What makes it easy for the servant are several things:

The first: that his disposition be soft, submissive, smooth, neither harsh nor hard, but yielding to it easily.

The second: that his faith be firm and his certainty strong, for this is the fruit and consequence of faith.

The third: the strength of his patience and steadfastness.

By these three matters he rises to this station and attaining it becomes easy for him. Deficiency and lagging in the soul regarding this arises from two things:

That the soul be rigid, not quick to grasp, but slow, hardly seeing the reality of a thing except after difficulty, and even if it sees it, it is accompanied by illusions, doubts, suspicions, and possibilities, so that seeing and clearly perceiving it is not freed for it.

The second: that the mind be keen and quick to comprehend, but the soul is weak and humble. When it sees truth and rectitude it becomes too weak to prefer them. Its possessor drives it like a sick, ailing person: every step he drives it, it stops after a step; or like driving a small child whose soul is attached to his desires and familiar things, so he drives him toward his rectitude while he turns to his play and games, and he follows only unwillingly. When the servant is granted a keen mind and a disposition that yields – if he restrains it, it restrains, and if he leads it, it follows easily, swiftly, and gently – and is supported with beneficial knowledge and firm faith, the streams of felicity come to him from every side.

Since these minds and dispositions belonged to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, and Allah perfected them for them through the light of Islam, the strength of certainty, and the direct experience of faith in their hearts, they were the best of all people after the prophets and messengers. And those after them, even if they spent the equivalent of Mount Uhud, would not reach a *mudd* (a measure) of one of them, nor half of it.

Whoever truly contemplates this matter will know from where deficiency and lagging come to him, and from where he advances, falls behind, and rises in the degrees of felicity. And success is from Allah. And Allah knows best.

**[Section: On the completeness of the love of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr) for him (ﷺ)]**

Among these is the completeness of al-Siddiq's love for him, and his aim to draw near to him and to gain his affection by every possible means. For this reason he begged al-Mughira to let him be the one to bring the Prophet (ﷺ) the good news of the arrival of the delegation of al-Ta'if, so that he would be the one who gave him the good news and delighted him with it. This indicates that it is permissible for a man to ask his brother to prefer him with one of the acts of devotion, and that it is permissible for a man to prefer his brother with it. The statement of those jurists who say that preference with acts of devotion is not permissible is not correct.

Aisha preferred Umar ibn al-Khattab with burial in her house beside the Prophet (ﷺ). Umar asked her for this, and she did not dislike his request nor did she dislike giving it.

On this basis, if a man asks another to prefer him with his place in the first row, the request is not disliked for him, nor is giving it disliked, nor are its like.

Whoever reflects on the biography of the Companions finds them neither disliking this nor refusing it. And is this anything but generosity, munificence, and preference over oneself with what is the greatest of one's beloved things, to delight one's Muslim brother, to honour his worth, to answer his request, and to encourage him toward good?

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 59, verse 9 (part 2 of 4):

And the reward of each of these qualities may outweigh the reward of that act of devotion (qurbah). In that case, one who prefers another in it is someone who has engaged in trade: he gives up one act of devotion and receives many times its worth. On this basis, there is nothing wrong with the owner of water preferring his brother with his water to perform wudu', while he himself performs tayammum (dry ablution with earth), if one of the two must perform tayammum. He has preferred his brother and gained both the virtue of preference (al-iithar) and the virtue of purification with earth. Neither the Book nor the Sunnah (the Prophetic example), nor the noble qualities of character, forbid this. On this basis, if a group is overcome by thirst and they face the prospect of death, and one of them has water, and he prefers others over himself and submits to death, this is permissible. It is not said that he has killed himself, nor that he has committed a prohibited act. Rather, this is the utmost of generosity and munificence, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾ [al-Hashr: 9]. This very thing occurred to a group of the Companions during the conquests of Syria, and it was counted among their virtues and excellences. Moreover, is not gifting the acts of devotion on which there is consensus and those on which there is disagreement to the deceased nothing but preferring him with their reward? And this is the very same as preferring others with acts of devotion. So what is the difference between preferring someone by performing an act on his behalf so that he may secure its reward, and performing it and then preferring him with its reward? And success is from Allah.

[Chapter: The Station of Preference]

Among the stations of "You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help" (﴿Iyyaka na'budu wa iyyaka nasta'in﴾) is the station of preference (al-iithar).

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul – it is those who are the successful﴾ [al-Hashr: 9].

Preference is the opposite of stinginess (al-shuhh). The one who prefers others over himself leaves what he himself needs.

The miser (al-shahih) is one who is greedy for what is not in his hand. When something comes into his hand, he is stingy with it and refuses to part with it. Thus miserliness (al-bukhl) is the fruit of stinginess, and stinginess commands miserliness, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Beware of stinginess, for stinginess destroyed those before you. It commanded them to be miserly, and they were miserly; it commanded them to sever ties, and they severed them."

So the miser is one who responds to the call of stinginess, and the one who prefers others is one who responds to the call of generosity.

Likewise, the generosity of not seeking what is in the hands of people is also a form of generosity, and it is superior to the generosity of giving.

'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak said: "The self's generosity in not seeking what is in people's hands is superior to the self's generosity in giving."

This station is the station of munificence, generosity and kindness. It is called the station of preference because it is its highest rank, for the ranks are three.

The first: that giving does not diminish him nor is it difficult for him. This is the station of generosity (al-sakha').

The second: that he gives more than half and leaves for himself something, or leaves an amount equal to what he has given. This is munificence (al-jud).

The third: that he prefers another with something while he himself is in need of it. This is the rank of preference (al-iithar). Its opposite is selfishness (al-athara), which is hoarding something from one's brother even though one is in need of it.

This is the rank about which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to the Ansar, may Allah be pleased with them: "You will encounter selfishness (athara) after me, so be patient until you meet me at the Basin (al-Hawd)." The Ansar are those whom Allah described with preference in His saying: ﴿And they prefer [others] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾.

Thus He described them with the highest ranks of generosity, and this was well known about them.

Qays ibn Sa'd ibn 'Ubadah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, was among the well-known generous men. Once he fell ill, and his brothers were slow to visit him.

He asked about them, and they said: "They were embarrassed because of the debt you owe them."

He said: "May Allah disgrace wealth that prevents brothers from visiting." Then he commanded a crier to announce: "Whoever has a debt owed to Qays, he is absolved of it."

Before evening came, the threshold of his door had been broken because of the large number of people who visited him.

One day they said to him: "Have you seen anyone more generous than you?" He said: "Yes. We stopped in the desert at the house of a woman, and her husband arrived. She said: 'Two guests have come to you.' So he brought a she-camel, slaughtered it, and said: 'Here, take it.' When the next day came, he brought another and slaughtered it. We said: 'We did not eat much of the one you slaughtered last night.' He said: 'I do not feed my guests what has spent the night.' So we stayed with him for two or three days, while it was raining, and he kept doing this. When we wanted to leave, we placed a hundred dinars in his house and said to the woman: 'Make our excuses to him.' Then we set off. At dawn, behold, a man was calling out behind us: 'Stop, you base caravan! Have you given me the price of my hospitality?' Then he caught up with us and said: 'You will either take it, or I will strike you with my spear.' So we took it, and he went back."

So reflect on the secret of divine decree, where the Wise, the All-Aware, may He be glorified, decreed that people should take precedence over the Ansar in worldly matters, while they (the Ansar) are the people of preference. This was so that He might reward them for their preferring their brothers over themselves in this world with high ranks in the Gardens of Eden above other people.

Then the virtue of their preference and its rank will become apparent, and whoever took precedence over them in worldly matters will envy them with the greatest envy. That is the bounty of Allah, which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.

So when you see people taking precedence over you, even though you are one of the people of preference, know that it is for a good that is intended for you. And Allah, the Exalted, knows best.

[Chapter: The Levels of Generosity]

Generosity (al-jud) has ten levels.

The first: generosity with the soul. This is its highest level, as the poet said:

"He gives of his soul when the miser withholds it, and generosity with the soul is the furthest extent of generosity."

The second: generosity with one's position (al-riyasah). This is the second level of generosity. The generous person's generosity leads him to humble his position, to be generous with it, and to prefer others in fulfilling the needs of the one who seeks.

The third: generosity with one's comfort, ease and rest, and the sacrifice of one's own relaxation. He gives of these while exhausted and toiling for the benefit of another. From this is a person's generosity with his sleep and pleasure for the sake of his night-companion, as it was said:

"Passionately devoted to generosity, if his petitioner said, 'Give me the sleep of your eyes,' he would not sleep."

The fourth: generosity with knowledge and its dissemination. This is among the highest levels of generosity, and generosity with it is superior to generosity with wealth, because knowledge is more noble than wealth.

People differ in their generosity with it according to varying levels, and the wisdom of Allah and His binding decree require that He never benefit a miser with it.

Among generosity with knowledge is that you give it to one who asks you about it, and even that you cast it upon him as a gift.

Among generosity with knowledge is that when a questioner asks you about an issue, you thoroughly answer it, giving a complete answer, not limiting your answer to what merely removes the immediate need. Some of them used to write in response to a fatwa only: "Yes," or "No," and nothing more.

I myself witnessed from Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, may Allah sanctify his soul, a remarkable thing in this regard:

Whenever he was asked about a legal question, he would mention, in answering it, the positions of the four Imams, when possible, the source of the disagreement, and the preference of the stronger opinion. He would mention related aspects of the question, which might be more beneficial to the questioner than his question itself. So his joy at those related aspects and implications would be greater than his joy at the question itself.

And these are his fatwas, may Allah have mercy on him, among the people. Whoever wishes to examine them will see this.

So from a person's generosity with knowledge is that he does not limit himself to the questioner's question, but mentions to him its equivalents, its related matters and its source, to the extent that it satisfies and suffices him.

The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the one who performs ablution with sea water. He said: "Its water is pure, and its dead animals are lawful." So he answered their question, and he was generous to them with what they may at times have needed more than what they asked about.

When they asked him about a ruling, he would draw their attention to its reason and wisdom. For example, they asked him about selling fresh dates (rutab) for dried dates (tamr). He said: "Do the fresh dates decrease when they dry?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then it is not permissible." The decrease of fresh dates upon drying was not hidden from him (ﷺ), but he drew their attention to the reason for the ruling. This is very common in his answers (ﷺ), such as his saying: "If you sell fruit to your brother, and then a calamity strikes it, it is not lawful for you to take anything from your brother's wealth. By what right does one of you take his brother's wealth unjustly?" And in another wording: "Do you see, if Allah withholds the fruit, by what right does one of you take his brother's wealth unjustly?" Thus he clarified the reason for which it is forbidden to compel him to pay the price, namely that Allah has withheld the fruit, in which the buyer has no part.

His opponents, meaning Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, used to criticize him for this. They would say: "A questioner asks him about the road to Egypt, for example, and he mentions along with it the road to Makkah, Madinah, Khurasan, Iraq and India. What need does the questioner have for that?"

By the life of Allah, that is not a fault. The fault is only ignorance and arrogance. This is the place of the well-known proverb:

"They called him 'the sour one,' though he is vinegar, like one who could not reach the bunch of grapes."

The fifth: generosity by benefiting others with one's standing (jah), such as intercession and walking with a man to a person of authority or the like. This is the zakat of standing, which the servant is required to give, just as teaching and imparting knowledge is its zakat.

The sixth: generosity with the benefit of the body in its various forms. As the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Every joint of one of you requires a charity each day the sun rises: to act justly between two people is a charity; to help a man with his mount, lifting him onto it or lifting his belongings onto it, is a charity; a good word is a charity; and every step one takes to prayer is a charity; and removing harm from the road is a charity." (Agreed upon.)

The seventh: generosity with one's honour, like the generosity of Abu Dhamdham, one of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them. He used to say each morning: "O Allah, I have no wealth to give in charity to the people, so I give them my honour as charity. Whoever insults me or slanders me, he is absolved." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Who among you can be like Abu Dhamdham?"

In this generosity there is great soundness of heart, peace of mind, and freedom from enmity with people.

The eighth: generosity with patience, forbearance and overlooking faults.

This is a noble level of generosity. It is more beneficial to its possessor than generosity with wealth, more honourable and more victorious for him, more able to control his soul, and more noble for it. Only great souls can attain it.

So whoever finds it difficult to be generous with his wealth should adopt this generosity, for he will reap the fruit of its praiseworthy consequences in this world before the Hereafter. This is the generosity of chivalry (futuwwah). Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And for wounds there is retaliation, but whoever forgoes it, it is an expiation for him﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 45]. And concerning this generosity, Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿The recompense for an evil is an evil like it, but whoever pardons and makes reconciliation, his reward is with Allah. Indeed, He does not love the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Shura: 40]. So in this verse He mentioned three stations: the station of justice, for which He gave permission; the station of virtue, to which He encouraged; and the station of wrongdoing, which He prohibited.

The ninth: generosity with good character, cheerfulness and openness. This is above generosity with patience, forbearance and pardon. It is what raises its possessor to the rank of one who fasts and stands in prayer at night. It is the heaviest thing placed in the Scale. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Do not belittle any act of kindness, even meeting your brother with a cheerful face." In this generosity is what it contains of benefits, joys, and various kinds of good. A servant cannot embrace people with his character and forbearance unless he has it.

The tenth: generosity by leaving what people have, so that one does not covet it. He does not turn his heart toward it, does not reach out for it with his heart, and does not pursue it with his state or his tongue. This is what 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak meant when he said it is superior to the self's generosity in giving.

The tongue of the state of destiny says to the poor, generous person: "If I do not give you what you can be generous with among people, then be generous to them by renouncing what is in their hands. Be favoured over them, outdo them in generosity, and be alone with ease away from them."

Each level of generosity has its own increase and its own particular effect on the heart and the state. And Allah, the Exalted, has guaranteed increase to the generous, and loss to the one who withholds. And Allah is the One whose help is sought.

[Chapter: The Meaning of Preference and Selfishness]

Chapter.

The author of "al-Manazil" (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

"Preference (al-iithar) is choosing and favouring. Selfishness (al-athara) is what is good when done willingly, and valid when done unwillingly."

The Shaykh distinguished between *ithar* (preferring others, altruism) and *athara* (selfishness, taking more than one's share), and made *ithar* a matter of choice, while *athara* is divided into the chosen and the compelled. The meaning of his words becomes clear through the difference between the two. *Ithar* is giving, and your singling out of the one you prefer over yourself. This can only be a matter of choice.

As for *athara*, it is the possessor of a thing claiming it for himself over you, taking it for himself and withholding it from you. The one who is preferred over is not praised for this, unless he does it willingly. For example, he is able to contest and wrestle for it, but does not do so, and leaves it and its taking to him willingly. This is good. If he is not able to do that, it is *athara* of compulsion.

By "validity" he means existence, i.e., it exists as something compelled. But it is only praiseworthy when it comes willingly from the one who is preferred over.

So the reality of *ithar* is the giving and bestowing of its owner, while *athara* is his substitution of the one preferred for the thing given. He leaves it, and what he has been substituted with, either willingly or unwillingly. It is as if you have preferred him by his taking, in that you left between him and it, and did not contest him.

ʿUbada ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "We pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to hear and obey, in hardship and ease, in what we like and dislike, and in *athara* over us, and that we would not dispute the command with its people." So hearing and obeying in hardship and ease, in what we like and dislike, is due to him, and to the imams after him. *Athara* here is not disputing the command with the imams after him in particular, for he (ﷺ) did not take more than his share over them.

[Section: The Degrees of *Ithar*]
[The First Degree: That you prefer creation over yourself]

He said: It has three degrees. The first degree: that you prefer creation over yourself in what does not cut off your religion, does not block your path, and does not corrupt your time.

That is: that you put them before yourself in their interests, for example that you feed them while you go hungry, clothe them while you go naked, give them drink while you remain thirsty, to the extent that this does not lead to committing a destruction that is not permitted in the religion. And for example, that you prefer them with your wealth while you sit down, a weary, compelled person, looking toward people or asking. Likewise, preferring them in anything that your religion forbids the one who prefers. That is foolishness and weakness, and the one who prefers in this is blamed before Allah and before people.

As for his saying "and does not block your path," it means it does not block your path of seeking and journeying toward Allah, the Exalted. For example, that you prefer your companion over your remembrance (of Allah), and your turning and gathering of yourself toward Allah. Then you have preferred him over Allah, and you have given away your share from Allah to something that does not deserve preference. Your situation is like that of a traveler proceeding on the road, whom a man meets and stops, and begins to talk to him and distract him until the caravan has passed him by. This is the state of most creation with the sincere one journeying toward Allah, the Exalted. Their preference over him is pure loss. How many are those who prefer something other than Allah over Him, and how few are those who prefer Allah over something else.

Likewise, preferring what corrupts the preferrer's time is also ugly. For example, that he gives up his time and scatters his heart in seeking a substitute, or prefers something by which he has gathered his heart and his concern upon Allah, so that he scatters his heart over it after its gathering, and disperses his thoughts. This too is *ithar* that is not praiseworthy.

Likewise, preferring others with occupying the heart and thought with their concerns and interests, which are not obligatory upon you, over beneficial reflection and the occupying of the heart with Allah. Comparable examples are not hidden. Indeed, this is the state of creation, and the dominant one among them.

Every cause that returns to you with the soundness of your heart, your time, and your state with Allah: do not prefer anyone over it. If you prefer it, you are preferring Satan over Allah, and you do not know.

Reflect on the situation of most creation in preferring, over Allah, those whose preference harms them and does not benefit them. What ignorance and foolishness is greater than this?

From this, the jurists spoke about *ithar* in acts of nearness (to Allah). They said it is disliked or forbidden, such as one who prefers another in the first row while he himself goes to the back, or prefers him with proximity to the imam on Friday, or prefers another with the adhan and iqama, or prefers him with knowledge that deprives him of himself, and raises the other over him, so that the other succeeds by it instead of him.

They also discussed ʿĀʾisha's (may Allah be pleased with her) preference of ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) in being buried beside the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in her chamber.

They answered this by saying that the dead person's deed is cut off by his death, and by his nearness. So *ithar* in nearness is not conceivable regarding him after death, since there is no drawing near on the part of the dead. Rather, this is preference in a noble, excellent dwelling for one who has more right to it than she does. So preferring with it is a nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, for the one who prefers. And Allah knows best.

[Section]
He said: It cannot be achieved except by three things: by magnifying the rights (of others), by abhorring stinginess (*shuhh*), and by desire for noble character.

This is a mention of what helps *ithar* and stirs it up. It is three things.

Magnifying the rights. Whoever has great regard for rights carries out their duties, observes them with their due observance, and considers their neglect a grave matter. He knows that if he does not reach the degree of *ithar*, he will not fulfill them as they should be fulfilled, so he makes his *ithar* a precaution for fulfilling them.

Second: abhorring stinginess. When he abhors and detests it, he commits to *ithar*, for he sees that there is no escape for him from this loathsome abhorrence except through *ithar*.

Third: desire for noble character. In proportion to his desire for it, his *ithar* will be. For *ithar* is the most excellent degree of noble character.

[Section: The Second Degree: Preferring the Pleasure of Allah over the Pleasure of Others]

He said: The second degree: preferring the pleasure of Allah over the pleasure of others, even if trials are great in it, and burdens heavy in it, and strength and body are weakened by it.

Preferring the pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, over others is that one wills and does what contains His good pleasure, even if it angers the creation. This is the degree of the prophets. The highest of it belongs to the Messengers, peace and blessings be upon them. The highest of that belongs to the Messengers of Firm Resolve among them. And the highest of all belongs to our Prophet (ﷺ), upon him and them. For he confronted the entire world, devoted himself to calling to Allah, endured the enmity of far and near for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, and preferred the pleasure of Allah over the pleasure of creation in every respect. The blame of any blamer did not take hold of him in preferring His pleasure. Rather, all his concern, resolve, and striving were focused on preferring the good pleasure of Allah, conveying His messages, raising His words, and fighting His enemies, until the religion of Allah prevailed over every religion, His proof was established over the worlds, and His blessing was completed upon the believers. So he conveyed the message, fulfilled the trust, advised the community, struggled for Allah with the struggle due to Him, and worshipped Allah until certainty came to him from his Lord. None attained from the degree of this *ithar* what he attained, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

As for his saying "even if trials are great in it, and burdens heavy in it":

The trial is great in it at first, so that whoever is not of its people falls back. But when he endures it and advances, those trials turn into gifts, and those burdens become help. This is known through personal and general experience. For no servant has preferred the good pleasure of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, over the good pleasure of creation, and borne its weight and burden, and been patient under its trial, except that Allah produces from that trial and burden a blessing and joy, and help in proportion to what he has borne for His good pleasure. So his fears turn into security, the places of his ruin into salvation, his fatigue into rest, his burden into help, his affliction into a blessing, his trial into a gift, and his wrath into good pleasure. So woe to the ones who lag behind, and woe to the cowards!

Furthermore, the sunna of Allah, which has no alteration, is that whoever prefers the pleasure of creation over His pleasure: He angers against him the one whose pleasure he sought, forsakes him on his side, and makes his trial at their hands. So the one who praised him becomes one who blames him. And whoever prefers His pleasure while they are angry: he has neither achieved his goal from them, nor reached the reward of the good pleasure of his Lord. And this is the most incapable and foolish of creatures.

Moreover, the pleasure of creation is neither attainable, nor commanded, nor transmitted. It is impossible. Rather, their anger against you is inevitable. So it is better that they be angry with you while you win the pleasure of Allah, than that they be pleased with you while Allah is not pleased with you. If their anger is inevitable in either case, then prefer the anger that brings the pleasure of Allah. If they are pleased with you after this, well and good; otherwise, the least harmful thing is the pleasure of one whose pleasure does not benefit you and whose anger does not harm your religion, your faith, or your afterlife. If it harms you in some small matter in this world, the harm of Allah's anger is greater and greater still.

Especially reason: bearing the lesser of two harms to repel the greater, and forgoing the lesser of two benefits to attain the greater. So weigh with your intellect, then see which of the two matters is better and prefer it, and which is worse and keep away from it. This is a definitive, self-evident proof for preferring the pleasure of Allah over the pleasure of creation.

Moreover, when he prefers the pleasure of Allah, Allah suffices him the burden of the anger of creation. And when he prefers their pleasure, they will not suffice him the burden of Allah's anger against him.

One of the early generations (*salaf*) said: "Pleasing one face is easier for you than pleasing many faces. If you please that one face, it will suffice you all the faces."

Al-Shafiʿi (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The pleasure of people is an unattainable goal. So hold to what is in the good of your soul, and keep to it."

It is known that there is no good for the soul except in preferring the pleasure of its Lord and Master over anything else.

Abu Firas (al-Hamdani) expressed this meaning well, though he did very badly in his words, since he says it to a created being who possesses neither benefit nor harm for himself or for anyone else:

> "Would that you were sweet, while life is bitter,
> and would that you were pleased, while people are angry.
> Would that what is between me and you were populated,
> and what is between me and all the worlds were ruined.
> When your love for me is sound, everything is easy,
> and all that is above the dust is (but) dust."

Then the Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned what makes this great *ithar* attainable. He said:

"This is attained by three things: by good return (*tayyib al-ʿawd*), by excellent Islam (*husn al-Islam*), and by strength of patience."

It is known that the one who prefers the pleasure of Allah is bound to face the enmity and harm of creation, and their efforts to destroy him, without doubt. This is the sunna of Allah in His creation. Otherwise, what was the fault of the prophets and messengers, and those who command justice among people, and those who uphold the religion of Allah and defend His Book and the Sunna of His Messenger in their eyes?

So whoever prefers the pleasure of Allah will inevitably be opposed by the scum and dregs of the world, the ignorant among them, the people of innovation and sin among them, the people of false leaderships, and everyone whose guidance opposes his guidance. None advances to oppose these except one seeking to return to Allah, one acting upon hearing the address: ﴿O soul at peace, return to your Lord, well-pleased and well-pleasing﴾ [al-Fajr: 27-28]. His Islam is a complete, firm backbone that men cannot shake and mountains cannot disturb, and the knot of his resolve in patience is firm, which trials, hardships, and fears cannot undo.

I say: The foundation of this lies in two matters: detachment from worldly life and seeking praise. Whoever weakens, and whoever falls behind, does so only from love of life and survival, and love of people's praise, and aversion to their blame. When he detaches himself from these two things, all obstacles fall away from him, and he then plunges into the ranks (of the struggle).

The foundation of these two things lies in two other things: the soundness of certainty and the strength of love.

The foundation of these two also lies in two other things: sincere turning and seeking, and striving for the causes that lead to them.

Here the knowledge and capacity of creation come to an end. Success thereafter is in the hand of the One in whose hand are the reins of all matters: ﴿And you do not will except that Allah wills; indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise. He admits whom He wills into His mercy, while for the wrongdoers He has prepared a painful punishment﴾ [al-Insan: 30-31].

[Section: The Third Degree: Preferring Allah's Preference]

He said: The third degree: preferring Allah's preference. For to engage in *ithar* is a claim of ownership. Then, leaving off witnessing your seeing of Allah's preference. Then, your absence from the leaving-off.

The Shaykh's phrase "the preference of God's preference" means that you attribute your preference to God and not to yourself. He is the One who alone holds preference, not you. It is as though you have handed preference over to Him. When you prefer someone else over yourself with something, the One who actually prefers is the Truth, not you. So He is the true Preferrer, since He is the true Giver.

Then the Shaykh explained the reason why it is correct to attribute preference to God and to withdraw it from yourself. He said: "Indeed, engaging in preference (al-ithar) is a claim of ownership (da'wa fi al-milk)."

When the servant claims that he is a preferrer, he has claimed ownership of what he has preferred over another. In reality, ownership belongs only to God, to whom everything belongs. When the servant withdraws from the claim of ownership, he has preferred God's preference, which is His giving, over his own preference. He witnesses that God alone is the Preferrer through His ownership. As for one who owns nothing, what preference does he have?

His saying: "Then the abandonment of witnessing your own vision of God's preference."

He means that when you prefer God's preference by handing over to Him the meaning of preference, a further remnant of yourself remains that you must leave behind. This is that you turn away from witnessing your vision that you preferred the Truth through your own preference, and that you attributed the preference to Him and not to yourself. In that witnessing and that vision of yours there is another claim, greater than the claim of ownership. It is that you claim that you have something which you preferred over God, and that you placed it before yourself in this, after it had been yours. This claim is harder than the first, because it includes what the first included of ownership, and adds to it the seeing of preference through it. The first is a claimant of ownership who prefers through it. This one is a claimant of ownership and a claimant of preference through it. Therefore he is obliged to abandon witnessing his vision of this preference. He should not believe that he preferred God with this preference. Rather, God is the One who has exclusively taken preference for Himself, since the preference is due to Him by His own obligation of it upon Himself, not by the servant's obligation of it to Him.

His saying: "Then your absence from the abandonment."

He means: when you descend from this witnessing and this vision, there remains in you another remnant.

It is your vision of this abandonment, which includes a claim that you own the abandonment. This is a false claim, since the servant has no share in the affair, and no act or omission is in his hand. The entire affair belongs to God.

It has been made clear in unveiling (kashf), witnessing (shuhud), knowledge (ilm), and gnosis (ma'rifa) that the servant has no possession at all, and the servant truly owns nothing. The true owner is only his Master. Thus preference, altruism, and exclusive appropriation (al-istithar) all belong to God, come from Him, and return to Him, whether the servant chooses and knows this, or is ignorant of it, or does not choose it. The preference occurs. Whether the servant dislikes it or is pleased with it, it is the exclusive appropriation of the Owner of the Truth through His ownership, exalted is He. From this I have understood His saying: "Indeed, preference is beautiful when willingly done, and valid even when done unwillingly."

And God, glorified and exalted, knows best.

(Section)

ʿAdī ibn Thābit said: In the time of the Children of Israel there was a monk (rāhib) who worshipped God, to the extent that madmen would be brought to him and he would seek refuge for them (yuʿawwiduhum), and they would be cured at his hands. A woman of noble standing among her people was brought to him; she had gone mad, and she had brothers. They brought her to him, and Satan kept adorning [the act] for him until he had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant. When her pregnancy became apparent, he kept frightening him and adorning for him the idea of killing her, until he killed her and buried her. Then Satan came in the form of a man to one of her brothers and informed him of what the monk had done. Then he went to the rest of her brothers one by one, and each man would meet his brother and say: "By God, someone came to me and told me something that greatly disturbed me to mention." Some of them mentioned it to others, until they brought the matter to their king. The people went to him and brought him down from his hermitage (ṣawma'a). He confessed to them what he had done, so he ordered that he be crucified. When he was raised upon the wood, Satan appeared to him and said: "I am the one who adorned this for you and cast you into it. Will you obey me in what I tell you, and I will free you?"

He said: "Yes."

[Satan] said: "Prostrate to me one prostration." So he prostrated to him, and the man was killed. This is the saying of God Most High: ﴿Like the Shayṭān when he says to man, "Disbelieve," then when he disbelieves, [the Shayṭān] says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾

(Benefit)

This context is not restricted to the one about whom this story is related; rather it is general for everyone who obeys Satan in his command to disbelief, so that he may help him and fulfil his need. Indeed, [Satan] disavows him and abandons him, just as he disavows all his allies in the Fire, and says to them: ﴿Indeed, I disbelieved in what you associated [with Allah] before.﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]

So he leads them to the worst of destinations, and disowns them completely.

(Section: On the Affliction of the Ignorant Worshipper)

As for the ignorant worshipper, his affliction comes from his turning away from knowledge and its rulings, and from the dominance of his imagination, his taste, his ecstasy, and what his soul desires. For this reason Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna and others said: "Beware of the trial of the corrupt scholar and the trial of the ignorant worshipper, for their trial is a trial for every person tried." This one, through his ignorance, averts [people] from knowledge and its requirements, and that one, through his transgression, calls to immorality. Allah, glorified is He, has struck the example of the other type with His saying: ﴿Like the Shayṭān when he says to man, "Disbelieve," then when he disbelieves, [the Shayṭān] says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds." (16) So the end of both of them is that they will be in the Fire, abiding therein eternally; and that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾

His story is well known: he built the foundation of his affair upon worship of Allah in ignorance, so Satan brought him down through his ignorance and made him disbelieve through his ignorance. Thus this is the leader of every ignorant worshipper who disbelieves without knowing, and that is the leader of every corrupt scholar who prefers the worldly life over the Hereafter.

Allah, glorified is He, has made the servant's contentment with this world, his tranquillity in it, and his heedlessness of recognising His signs, reflecting upon them, and acting by them, the cause of his misery and destruction. These two things—contentment with the world and heedlessness of the Lord's signs—do not come together except in a heart that does not believe in the Return and does not hope to meet the Lord of the worlds. Otherwise, if his foot were firmly planted in faith in the Return, he would not be content with this world, nor would he be at rest in it, nor would he turn away from the signs of Allah.

When you contemplate the conditions of people, you will find that this type is the predominant one among people, and they are the cultivators of this world. The people who are the exception and fewest in number are those who are contrary to this; they are the most strangers among them. They have a station and their station is theirs; their knowledge is other than their knowledge, their will is other than their will, and their path is other than their path. He is in one valley and they are in another valley. God Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who do not hope for meeting Us, and are pleased with the life of this world and are content with it, and those who are heedless of Our signs—those, their abode is the Fire because of what they used to earn.﴾ Then He mentioned the description of the opposite of these, and their final destiny and outcome, with His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds—their Lord guides them by their faith; rivers flow beneath them in Gardens of Bliss.﴾ So these, their faith in meeting Allah bequeathed to them non-attachment to the world, tranquillity not founded in it, and constant remembrance of His signs.

So these are the inheritances of faith in the Return, and those are the inheritances of not believing in it and heedlessness of it.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah al-Hashr, verses 18–19 (Part 1 of 3)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾

These people forgot their souls not in every respect, but in the respect through which their welfare, perfection and happiness are attained. They did not forget them in the respect through which lies their appetite, their share and their desires. So He caused them to forget the welfare of their souls, such that they neither performed nor sought it, and to forget their faults and deficiencies, such that they neither removed nor avoided them. And He caused them to forget the perfection for which their souls were created, so they neither knew it nor sought it. Thus they are ignorant of the realities of their own souls from this standpoint, even though they know them from other standpoints.

(Benefit)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾

He punished them for their forgetting Him by causing them to forget themselves. So they forgot the welfare of their souls, that they should perform it, and their faults, that they should correct them, and their shares, that they should take them. Among the greatest of the welfare of the soul and the most beneficial of its shares is its remembrance of its Lord and Originator. It has no bliss, no joy, no success and no righteousness except through remembering Him, loving Him, obeying Him, turning towards Him and turning away from all else. So He caused them to forget that, because they had forgotten Him, and this forgetting produced in them another forgetting. This is the opposite of the state of those who remembered Him and did not forget. Their remembrance of Him made them mindful of the welfare of their souls, so they performed it. It made them aware of their faults, so they corrected them. It made them recognise their lofty shares, so they hastened towards them. Thus He recompensed those (who remembered Him) for their remembrance by causing them to remember faith, its love, its remembrance and its gratitude. When their hearts were emptied of that, they found no escape from its opposite.

This shows you the perfection of His justice, may He be glorified, in decreeing disbelief and sins upon them. If His decree upon them of disbelief and sins is justice from Him towards them, then His decree of punishment upon them is more just and even more just. He, may He be glorified, executes His judgement upon His servant, and His judgement in it is just.

He has in this two decrees: the decree of the cause and the decree of the effect. Both are just. When the servant abandoned His remembrance and abandoned doing what He loves, He punished him by causing him to forget himself. This forgetting brought about in him the commission of what He hates and what displeases Him, by His decree which is just. So there followed for him, because of this doing and abandoning, punishments and pains from which he had no escape. Rather, they follow upon it as effects follow their causes. So this is pure justice from the Lord, may He be exalted. He is just towards the servant at the beginning and at the end. He is good in His justice, beloved in it and praised for it, and whoever is treated justly by Him, willingly or unwillingly, praises Him for it.

Al-Hasan said: "They entered the Fire, and yet His praise was in their hearts, though they found no way to it."

(Benefit)

The saying of Allah, the Exalted, indicates the obligation of self-examination: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow.﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]

He, may He be exalted, says: Let each one of you look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection of deeds: are they of the righteous deeds that will save him, or of the evil deeds that will destroy him?

Qatadah said: "Your Lord has never ceased to bring the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow."

The point is that the soul's righteousness comes through self-examination, and its corruption comes through neglecting it and drifting along with it.

(Benefit)

As for the acknowledgement of the Creator, it is a necessary, innate knowledge for the human being. No one is so heedless of it that he does not know it. Rather, he must have known it, even if it is supposed that he has forgotten it. For this reason, informing a person of it is called "reminding" (tadhkir), since it is a reminder of innate, necessary knowledge. The servant may forget it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

In the authentic hadith: "Allah says to the disbeliever: 'Today I forget you as you forgot Me.'"

(Section)

Here is a matter that must be noticed: the Lord, may He be exalted, testified to the truth of what He reported. He is the most truthful of the truthful. He swore an oath upon it, and He is the most sincere of those who swear. He confirmed it by comparing it to what is actual, which admits no doubt in any way. He established upon it such evidences, both visible and demonstrative, that He made it witnessed and seen through insight, even if it is not seen with the eyes. Yet most souls are heedless of it. They do not prepare for it and do not take up its readiness. Those who prepare for it and take up its readiness are only single individuals here and there. Most of creation does not reflect on the purpose of their being brought into being and sent out into this abode. They do not reflect on the brevity of their stay in the house of delusion, nor on their departure and transfer from it, nor where they will journey and where they will settle. Sense has taken possession of them, the share of intellect in them is small, heedlessness has overwhelmed them, and the wishes that are like a mirage have deceived them, and long hope has tricked them. It is as if the one who remains will never depart, and as if one of them will never be resurrected or questioned. It is as if with every resident there is a decree from Allah to so-and-so son of so-and-so, granting him security from His punishment and success in His abundant reward.

As for sensual pleasures and soul-appetites, however they are obtained and from whatever direction they appear, they take hold of them, heedless of being called to account, secure from the consequence. They strive for what they can attain and leave what they are responsible for. They build up what they are about to leave, and ruin what they are about to arrive at. They are heedless of the Hereafter. The desires of their souls have distracted them, so they do not look at its welfare, nor do they set about gathering its provision for its journey. ﴿They forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

How utterly strange is the heedlessness of one whose moments are counted and whose breaths are numbered, while the mounts of night and day hasten him along, and yet he does not reflect where he is being carried or to what station he is being conveyed:

How can the eye sleep while it is at ease, when it does not know in which of the two abodes it will descend?

When death comes upon one of them, he is anxious about the ruin of his self and the loss of his pleasures, not about his past offences, nor about the evil of his final destination after death. If a thought of that occurs to one of them, he relies upon pardon or mercy, and he is certain that this is his lot, without doubt. If the intelligent person had summoned his mind, and what his intellect had summoned, and had journeyed with his thought, looked intently, and reflected upon the signs to understand the purpose of his creation, then the eye of the one who is departing would have looked at the road, the traveller would have taken provision, the sick would have sought treatment, and the prudent would have prepared for what may come.

So what is the assumption about a matter that is certain, as surely as the truthfulness of his faith and the strength of their certainty? It is as if they are witnessing the matter. The abodes of faith have become empty of their people, and its landmarks lie in ruin upon their foundations.

Ibn Wahb said: Muslim ibn Ali informed me, from al-Awza'i, who said:
"When the dawn broke, or before it, the early generations were as if birds were perched upon their heads, turning towards themselves. If a beloved of one of them had been absent for a while and then returned, he would not turn to him. They continued in this state until sunrise. Then some of them would rise and go to others, and they would begin with what most needed their attention concerning the affair of their return and what they were heading towards. Then they would turn to jurisprudence."

(Section)

Know that constant remembrance of the Lord, blessed and exalted, necessitates security from forgetting Him, which is the cause of the servant's wretchedness in his livelihood and in his return. For the forgetting of the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, necessitates the forgetting of one's own self and its welfare. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

When the servant forgets himself, he turns away from its welfare, forgets it, and busies himself away from it, so it perishes and is corrupted, without doubt. Like one who has a crop, a garden or livestock, or something else whose welfare and success depend on his tending and caring for it, but he neglects it, forgets it and busies himself with other things, and so loses its welfare. It will certainly be corrupted.

This is the case even though another can take his place in caring for it. So what is the assumption about the corruption, destruction and wretchedness of one's own self, when he neglects and forgets it, busies himself away from its welfare, disables its care, and abandons the tending that would set it right? Whatever corruption, destruction, failure and deprivation you wish for, it will come.

This is the one whose whole affair has become neglected: his affair has slipped from his hands, his welfare has been lost, and the causes of ruin, failure and destruction surround him.

There is no way to be secure from that except by constant remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, and by keeping it always upon the tongue, so that the tongue never ceases to be moist with it. And that He be placed in the position of the servant's life, upon which he cannot do without. And in the position of his food, which if he lacks it, his body is corrupted and perishes. And in the position of water in severe thirst, and in the position of clothing in heat and cold, and in the position of shelter in the severity of winter and the scorching wind.

It is fitting for the servant to give the remembrance of Allah this position and even greater. For where is the ruin and corruption of the spirit and the heart compared to the ruin and corruption of the body?

That bodily ruin is unavoidable, and it may be followed by a righteousness that is also unavoidable. But the ruin of the heart and spirit is a ruin after which no righteousness or success is hoped for. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty.

[Section: Sins cause one to forget Allah]

Among their punishments is that they call for Allah's forgetting of His servant, leaving him, abandoning him, and leaving him between himself and his devil. There is the ruin after which no salvation is hoped for. Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do. And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hashr: 18–19]

So He commanded them to be mindful of Him, and forbade His believing servants from resembling those who forgot Him by abandoning His mindfulness. He informed them that He punishes whoever abandons mindfulness by causing him to forget himself, that is, causing him to forget its welfare, what saves it from His punishment, what brings it eternal life, and the perfection of its delight, joy and bliss. So Allah causes him to forget all of that, as recompense for his forgetting of His greatness, His fear, and attending to His command. You see the disobedient neglecting his soul's welfare and wasting it. Allah has made his heart heedless of His remembrance, and he has followed his desire, and his affair has become neglected. The welfare of his worldly life and his Hereafter has slipped from him. He has squandered his eternal happiness and exchanged it for the lowest of pleasures, which are only a summer cloud or the fancy of a phantom, as it has been said:

Dreams of sleep, or like a passing shadow; the intelligent person is not deceived by the like of them.

The greatest of punishments is the servant's forgetting of his own self, his neglecting of it, and his squandering of its portion and share from Allah. He sells that for deception, humiliation, and the most meagre price. He wastes the One without whom he has no sufficiency, and for whom there is no substitute, and he exchanges Him for one from whom comes all sufficiency, or from whom comes every substitute:

Whatever you lose of anything, it has a substitute; but there is no substitute for what you lose of Allah.

So Allah, may He be glorified, substitutes for everything else, and nothing can substitute for Him. He suffices in place of everything, and nothing suffices in His place. He grants protection from everything, and nothing grants protection from Him. He withholds from everything, and nothing withholds from Him. How can the servant be independent of obedience to one whose state is such, even for the blink of an eye?

How can he forget His remembrance and waste His command, until He causes him to forget himself, so that he loses it and wrongs it with the greatest wrong?

The servant did not wrong his Lord, but he wronged himself; and his Lord did not wrong him, but it is he who wronged himself.

[Section: Disobedience causes the servant to forget himself]

Among its punishments is that it causes the servant to forget himself. When he forgets himself, he neglects it, corrupts it and destroys it. If it is asked: How can the servant forget himself? And if he forgets himself, what does he remember? What is the meaning of his forgetting himself?

It is said: Yes, he forgets himself with the greatest forgetting. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

When they forgot their Lord, may He be glorified, He forgot them and caused them to forget themselves, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67]

So He, may He be glorified, punished whoever forgot Him with two punishments:

The first: that He forgot him.
The second: that He caused him to forget himself.

His forgetting of the servant, may He be glorified, means His neglect, His abandonment, His leaving him, and His squandering of him. Then ruin is nearer to him than the hand is to the mouth. As for His causing him to forget himself, it means that He causes him to forget its lofty shares, the causes of its happiness, its success and its righteousness, and what it is perfected by. By forgetting all of that, it does not come to his mind, he does not make it the object of his remembrance, and he does not direct his resolve towards it so as to desire it. For it does not pass through his mind until he intends it and prefers it.

Furthermore, He causes him to forget the faults, deficiencies and afflictions of his soul, so the thought of removing them does not occur to him.

Furthermore, He causes him to forget the diseases of his soul and heart and their pains, so the thought of treating them does not occur to his heart, nor the effort to remove their ailments and diseases, which lead to corruption and ruin. He is sick, overwhelmed by the disease, and his disease is moving towards destruction, yet he is not aware of his sickness, and the thought of treating it does not occur to his mind. This is among the greatest of punishments, both general and particular.

What punishment could be greater than that of one who neglects and wastes his soul, forgets its welfare, its disease and its remedy, and the causes of its happiness, success, righteousness and eternal life in enduring bliss? Whoever reflects on this point will see clearly that most of these people have forgotten the reality of their souls, wasted them, and squandered their share from Allah. They have sold them cheaply for a meagre price, in a sale of deception. This will only become apparent to them at death, and it will become fully apparent on the Day of Mutual Deception (Yawm al-Taghabun), the day when the servant will realise that he was deceived in the contract he made for his soul in this abode, and in the trade in which he traded for his return. For everyone trades in this world for his Hereafter.

Those who lose, who think that they are the people of profit and gain, have bought the life of this world, with their share and their pleasures in it, at the price of the Hereafter and their share in it. So they have squandered their good things in their worldly life and enjoyed them, and were content with them and at rest with them. Their striving was for obtaining them. So they sold, bought and traded, and they exchanged the deferred for the immediate, credit for cash, and the absent for the present. They said: "This is prudence." One of them says:

Take what you see, and leave what you have only heard of.

How then should I sell a present, cash, witnessed thing in this abode for an absent thing on credit in another abode other than this one? To this is added the weakness of faith, the strength of the call of desire, love of the immediate, and imitating the sons of the same kind. Most of creation is in this losing trade, concerning which Allah said about its people: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 86]
