And He said about them: ﴿So their trade did not profit them, nor were they guided.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16]

So when the Day of Mutual Deception comes, the loss in this trade will become apparent to them, and souls will be torn apart by regret over them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 59, verses 18–19 (part 2 of 3):

As for the winners, they sold the perishable for the everlasting, the base for the precious, and the trivial for the magnificent. They said: "What is the worth of this world, from its beginning to its end, that we should sell our share of Allah the Exalted and the Last Abode for it? How can a servant obtain from it in this short time, which in reality is like the nap of a dream, and which has no relation whatsoever to the Abode of Permanence?" Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of [one] day, knowing each other [in recognition] among themselves﴾ [Yunus: 45].

Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what [position] are you to mention it? To your Lord is its finality. You are only a warner for those who fear it. It will be, on the day they see it, as if they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42–46].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day. [This is] notification﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth in number of years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who keep count." He will say, "You remained not but a little, if you had only known"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112–114].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The day the Horn is blown, and We gather the criminals that day, blue-eyed, whispering among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days]." We are most knowing of what they say when they of best course will say, "You remained not but a day"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102–104].

This, then, is the reality of the world when the Day of Resurrection arrives. When they knew how brief their stay in it had been, and that for them there is another abode besides this abode, namely the abode of life and the abode of permanence, they saw that selling the abode of permanence for the abode of perishing is among the greatest deceptions. So they traded the trade of the discerning, and were not deceived by the trade of the foolish among people. Thus, on the Day of Mutual Deception, the profit of their trade and the value of what they had bought became manifest to them. Every person in this world is a seller, a buyer and a trader, and every person goes forth in the morning, selling his soul; either he frees it or he destroys it.

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. A true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111].

This is the first installment of the price of this trade. So trade, O bankrupt ones, and you who cannot afford this price: here is another price. If you are of the people of this trade, then give this price: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the travelers, the bowers, the prostrators, those who enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits of Allah. And give good tidings to the believers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112].

﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [It is that] you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Saff: 10–11].

The point is that sins make the servant forget his share of this profitable trade and occupy him with the losing trade, and that alone is sufficient as a punishment. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: The Station of Self-Accounting]
[From the station of self-accounting, the station of repentance becomes valid for him]

Section: The Station of Self-Accounting

Let us return to the mention of the stations of "﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾", which a servant does not belong to until he descends into its stations.

We have mentioned from among them alertness, insight, reflection and resolve.

These four stations are, for all the other stations, like a foundation for a building, and upon them depend the stations of the journey to Allah. The journey to Him cannot be conceived without descending into them at all. They follow the order of physical travel: the one who resides in his homeland cannot undertake a journey until he awakens from his heedlessness regarding the journey; then he gains insight into the matter of his journey and its danger, and what benefit and advantage it holds for him; then he reflects on the preparations for the journey, the provisions, and the readying of its equipment; then he resolves upon it. When he has resolved and gathered his intention, he moves to the station of self-accounting, which is distinguishing between what is his and what is owed by him. So he keeps what is his and discharges what he owes, because he is a traveler on a journey from which none returns.

From the station of self-accounting, the station of repentance becomes valid for him, because when he takes account of himself, he recognizes what right is upon him, so he leaves it and is absolved of it before its owner. This is the reality of repentance, so placing self-accounting before it is more appropriate.

There is also a reason for placing repentance before it: self-accounting is not valid except after repentance is sound.

The truth is that repentance lies between two self-accountings: a self-accounting before it, which requires it, and a self-accounting after it, which requires its preservation. Repentance is thus framed by two self-accountings. Allah's saying indicates self-accounting: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]. So Allah the Glorified commanded the servant to look at what he has sent forward for tomorrow, and this includes taking account of himself regarding it and looking into whether what he has sent forward is fit for him to meet Allah with, or is not fit.

The purpose of this looking is what it necessitates and requires of complete preparation for the Day of Return, and the sending forward of what saves him from the punishment of Allah and whitens his face before Allah. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and adorn yourselves for the Great Exposure: ﴿On that Day you will be exhibited; not a secret of yours will be concealed﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18]," or he said: "before the One to whom your deeds are not hidden."

[Pillars of Self-Accounting]
[The First Pillar: Comparison between what belongs to the servant and what belongs to Allah]

The author of the Manazil said: Self-accounting has three pillars.

The first of them: that you compare between His blessing and your offence.

That is, you compare what is from Allah and what is from you. Then the disparity becomes evident to you, and you know that there is nothing but His pardon and His mercy, or else destruction and ruin.

Through this comparison you know that the Lord is Lord and the servant is servant, the reality of the self and its attributes becomes clear to you, along with the greatness of the majesty of Lordship, and the Lord's uniqueness in perfection and bounty, and that every blessing from Him is a favour and every affliction from Him is justice. Before this comparison you were ignorant of the reality of your self and of the lordship of its Originator and Creator. When you compare, it becomes apparent to you that the self is the source of every evil and the foundation of every deficiency, that its limit is ignorance and wrongdoing, and that were it not for Allah's favour and mercy in purifying it, it would never have been purified; and were it not for His guidance, it would never have been guided; and were it not for His direction and success, it would never have reached any good at all. The attainment of that by the self comes from its Creator and Originator, and its dependence upon Him is like the dependence of its existence upon His bringing it into being. Just as the self has no existence from itself, so it has no perfection of existence from itself; it has nothing from itself but non-existence: non-existence of essence and non-existence of perfection. At that point you truly say: "I acknowledge Your blessing upon me, and I acknowledge my sin."

Then you compare between the good deeds and the bad deeds, and through this comparison you know which of the two is greater and weightier in quantity and quality.

This second comparison is a comparison between your actions and what is solely from yourself.

He said: This comparison is difficult for one who lacks three things: the light of wisdom, a low opinion of the self, and the ability to distinguish blessing from trial.

That is, this comparison and self-accounting depend upon the light of wisdom, which is the light with which Allah illuminated the hearts of the followers of the Messengers. By its measure you perceive the disparity and become able to take account.

The light of wisdom here is the knowledge by which the servant distinguishes between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, the harmful and the beneficial, the complete and the deficient, good and evil, and by which he perceives the ranks of deeds, the preferred and the disfavoured, the accepted and the rejected. The more his share of this light, the more complete and perfect his share of self-accounting.

As for a low opinion of the self, one needs it because a good opinion of the self prevents thorough scrutiny and confuses him, so he sees faults as virtues and defects as perfections, for the one who loves sees the faults of his beloved in the same way.

"The eye of contentment is blind to every flaw, just as the eye of anger reveals all the faults."

None thinks ill of himself except one who knows himself, and whoever thinks well of himself is among the most ignorant of people about himself.

As for distinguishing blessing from trial: he must differentiate between the blessing through which kindness and gentleness are seen, and through which he is assisted in attaining his eternal happiness, and the blessing through which gradual enticement is seen. How many are led on gradually by blessings while unaware, enchanted by the praise of the ignorant, deceived by Allah's granting of his needs and His concealing of him! Most of creation think that these three are signs of happiness and success; that is the extent of their knowledge.

When these three are complete in him, he then knows that whatever blessings of Allah upon him are gathered toward Allah are a true blessing, and whatever He has separated from him and taken from him is trial in the form of blessing and affliction in the form of gift. So let him beware, for he is being led on gradually. He should also distinguish between favour and proof, for how often one of them is confused for the other! The servant is between a favour from Allah upon him and a proof from Him against him, and he is never free of both. The religious command contains both His favour and His proof. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164]. He says: ﴿Rather, Allah confers favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17]. He says: ﴿So to Allah belongs the conclusive argument﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

The cosmic command also contains His favour and His proof. When He decrees for him, in the cosmic sense, a decree accompanied by the connection of the religious command to it, it is a favour upon him; and if it is not accompanied by the religious command, it is a proof against him.

Likewise, His religious command, when connected to His cosmic decree, his being granted the ability to fulfil it is a favour from Him upon him; and if it is stripped of His cosmic decree, it becomes a proof against him. Favour lies in the conjunction of one of the two commands with the other, and proof lies in the separation of one from the other. Thus every knowledge accompanied by a deed that pleases Allah the Glorified is a favour, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every power, outward and inward, accompanied by the execution of His pleasure and commands is a favour, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every state accompanied by an effect in supporting His religion and calling to it is a favour from Him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every wealth joined with spending in the way of Allah and in obedience to Him, seeking neither reward nor thanks, is a favour from Allah upon him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every free time joined with occupation in what the Lord desires from His servant is a favour upon him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every acceptance among people, and every honour and love directed toward him, when connected with humility before the Lord, lowliness and brokenness, awareness of the defect of the self and of one's deeds, and offering sincere advice to creation, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every insight and admonition, reminder and instruction from the Truth, the Glorified, to the servant, when connected with lessons, an increase in reason, and knowledge in faith, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every state with Allah the Exalted, or station connected with journeying to Allah and preferring His desire over the servant's desire, is a favour from Allah. But if it is accompanied by halting at it and contentment with it, and preferring its requirement out of the pleasure of the self in it, its calm in it and its inclination toward it, it is a proof from Allah against him.

So let the servant contemplate this most momentous place, and distinguish between the positions of favours and trials, and proofs and blessings. How often does this become confused for the elite of people and the practitioners of the spiritual path! And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

[Section: The Second Pillar: Distinguishing between what is for the servant and what is upon him]

Section

The second pillar of the pillars of self-accounting is: that you distinguish what is due to the Truth upon you, and between what is yours and what is upon you, of the obligations of servitude, the commitment to obedience, and the avoidance of

...disobedience, and between what is yours and what is upon you. What is yours is the lawfully permissible (mubah shar'i). Upon you is a right, and you have a right. So fulfil what is upon you, and it will give you what is yours.

It is necessary to distinguish between what is yours and what is upon you, and to give every person with a right his right.

Many people treat much of what is their duty as falling under what is optional for them. They therefore hesitate between doing and not doing it, and if they do it, they regard it as a supererogatory favour they have performed, not a right they have discharged.

Opposite these are those who regard much of what is optional for them to do or leave as falling under what is their duty to do or leave. So they worship God by abandoning what is permitted to them to do, as in abandoning many lawful things, and they think this is obligatory upon them. Or they worship God by doing what is permitted to them to leave, and they think this is obligatory upon them.

An example of the first kind is someone who worships God by abstaining from marriage, or from eating meat, or fruit, for example, or from good foods and clothing. Out of ignorance, he regards this as something required of him, so he makes it obligatory upon himself to abstain, or he considers abstaining from it to be among the best acts of drawing near to God and the most excellent acts of obedience. The Prophet ﷺ rejected this view held by some people. In the Sahih it is reported that a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ asked about his worship in private, and they seemed to belittle it. One of them said: "As for me, I will not eat meat." Another said: "As for me, I will not marry women." Another said: "As for me, I will not sleep on a bed." When the Prophet ﷺ heard of their statement, he delivered a sermon and said: "What is the matter with people who say, 'As for me, I will not eat meat,' and another says, 'As for me, I will not marry,' and another says, 'As for me, I will not sleep on a bed'? But I marry women, I eat meat, I sleep and I pray at night, I fast and I break my fast. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah (way), he is not of me." So he disassociated himself from those who turned away from his Sunnah, and they worshipped God by abandoning what He had permitted His servants of good things, out of aversion to it, believing that aversion to it and forsaking it is worship. This person did not distinguish between what is upon him and what is his.

An example of the second kind is someone who worships God through innovated acts of worship (bid'ah, innovation in religion), which he believes bring about spiritual states, unveiling, and the power to influence. These matters have necessary consequences that cannot occur at all without them. So he commits himself to observing those consequences by doing or abstaining, and he regards them as a right owed to God upon him, while in fact they are a right for him, and he may leave them. This is like the spiritual exercises and the practices that many wayfarers have laid down according to their own tastes, ecstasies, and terminologies, without distinguishing between what in them is the servant's own portion and what is the right God has upon him. This is one kind, and that is another kind.

[Section: The Third Pillar: Being Pleased with Obedience and Reproaching Oneself for Disobedience]

Among the pillars of self-accounting is what the author of al-Manazil (Abu Isma'il al-Harawi) mentioned. He said:

"The third: that you know that every act of obedience you are pleased with from yourself is against you, and every sin for which you reproach your brother is against you (lit. 'comes to you')."

A servant's being pleased with his obedience is a sign of his good opinion of himself, his ignorance of the rights of servanthood, and his failure to act in the way that the Lord, may His majesty be exalted, deserves and that it is fitting to treat Him.

The sum of this is that his ignorance of himself, its attributes, its afflictions, and the defects of his deeds, along with his ignorance of his Lord, His rights, and what He deserves to be treated with, gives rise to his being pleased with his obedience and having a good opinion of it. From this arise vanity, arrogance, and afflictions greater than the major visible sins such as adultery, drinking wine, fleeing from battle, and the like.

So being pleased with obedience is among the follies and foolishness of the soul.

Those of resolve and insight are the most diligent in seeking forgiveness after acts of obedience, because they witness their own shortcomings in them, and their failure to stand before God in them as befits His majesty and greatness. They know that had it not been for the command, none of them would have undertaken such worship, nor would God have been pleased with it for His Master.

God Most High commanded His delegation and the pilgrims to His House to seek His forgiveness after they depart from Arafat, which is the greatest and most excellent of the standing places. He said: ﴿So when you depart from Arafat, remember Allah at the Sacred Monument. And remember Him as He has guided you, although you were before it among those astray. Then depart from where the people depart and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 198-199]

He Most High also said: ﴿And those who seek forgiveness before dawn.﴾ [Al-Imran: 17]

Al-Hasan said: "They extended the prayer until the pre-dawn, then they sat seeking forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

In the Sahih, it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ, when he finished the prayer, would seek forgiveness three times, then say: "O Allah, You are As-Salam (Peace), and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour."

God Most High commanded him to seek forgiveness after fulfilling the message, after discharging what was upon him of its burdens, after performing the obligatory Hajj, and as his end drew near. He said at the end of a surah revealed to him: ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt with the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ [An-Nasr: 1-3]

From here, Umar and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, understood that this was the announcement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's death, which Allah had informed him of. So He commanded him to seek His forgiveness after completing what was upon him. It was as if it were a notification: "You have discharged what was upon you, and nothing remains upon you, so let your conclusion be seeking forgiveness," just as it was the conclusion of the prayer, the Hajj, and the night prayer. The conclusion of ablution as well is that one says after finishing: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance. O Allah, make me of those who repent often, and make me of those who purify themselves."

This is the attitude of one who knows what is due to God and fitting to His majesty of the rights and conditions of servanthood, not the ignorance of those who make claims and their wild utterances.

Some of the knowers of God said: "Whenever you are pleased with yourself and your deed for God's sake, know that He is not pleased with it. Whoever knows that his soul is the abode of every fault and evil, and that his deed is exposed to every blight and deficiency, how could he be pleased with his soul and his deed for God?"

How excellent is the statement of Shaykh Abu Madyan, when he says: "Whoever realises servanthood sees his actions with the eye of hypocrisy (riya'), his states with the eye of pretension, and his words with the eye of fabrication. Whenever the sought object becomes great in your heart, your self becomes small in your eyes, and the price you pay to obtain it becomes insignificant. Whenever you witness the reality of lordship and the reality of servanthood, and you know God and you know the self, and it becomes clear to you that the merchandise you have does not suit the True King, and even if you came with the deeds of both jinn and humankind you would fear their consequence, He accepts it only by His generosity, bounty, and grace, and He rewards you for it also by His generosity, bounty, and grace."

As for his saying: "Every sin for which you reproach your brother is against you (comes to you)," it may mean: that it will inevitably come to you and you will commit it. This is derived from the hadith that al-Tirmidhi reported in his Jami' from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever reproaches his brother for a sin, he will not die until he commits it."

Imam Ahmad said, explaining this hadith: "[That is] for a sin from which he has already repented."

Also, in reproaching there is a hidden kind of gloating over the one who is reproached.

In al-Tirmidhi also, it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not display gloating toward your brother, lest Allah have mercy on him and test you."

It may also mean: that your reproaching your brother for his sin is greater in sinfulness than his sin, and worse than his disobedience, because it contains the boldness of obedience, the self-praise of the soul, the thanking of it, and proclaiming it free from sin while your brother has been afflicted by it. Perhaps his being broken by his sin, the humiliation and submission it produced in him, his belittling of himself, and his freeing himself from the disease of self-claim, pride, and self-admiration, and his standing before God with bowed head, lowered gaze, and broken heart, is more beneficial to him and better than the boldness of your obedience, your multiplying it and counting on it, and your taking favour with God and His creation because of it. How near this disobedient one is to the mercy of God, and how near this one who boasts is to God's wrath! A sin by which you are humbled before Him is more beloved to Him than an act of obedience by which you boast before Him. Your sleeping and waking up regretful is better than your spending the night standing in prayer and waking up self-admiring, for the self-admirer, his deed does not ascend. And your laughing while acknowledging your fault is better than your weeping while boasting. The moaning of sinners is more beloved to God than the chanting of the glorifiers who boast. Perhaps God gave him this sin as a remedy to draw out a deadly disease that is in you without your noticing.

God has secrets concerning those who obey Him and those who disobey Him that no one knows but Him, and only people of insight perceive them, so they know of them as much as human knowledge can attain. Beyond that is what the noble recording angels do not perceive. The Prophet ﷺ said: "If the slave-woman of one of you commits fornication, let him impose the prescribed punishment upon her and not reproach her (la yuthrib)." That is, he should not reproach her, from the words of Yusuf, peace be upon him, to his brothers: ﴿No reproach will there be upon you today.﴾ [Yusuf: 92] Indeed, the scale is in the hand of God, and the judgment belongs to God. So the whip with which this disobedient one is struck is in the hand of the Turner of hearts. The intent is to enforce the legal punishment, not to reproach or rebuke. No one feels secure from the turns of destiny and its assault except those ignorant of God. God Most High said to the most knowing of creation of Him and the closest of them to Him in means: ﴿And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.﴾ [Al-Isra: 74] And Yusuf the truthful said: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plot, I would incline toward them and be among the ignorant.﴾ [Yusuf: 33]

The common oath of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was: "No, by the Turner of hearts."

He also said: "There is no heart but that it is between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it firm, He makes it firm, and if He wills to make it swerve, He makes it swerve." Then he said: "O Allah, Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion. O Allah, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience."

**Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on Surah al-Hashr, verses 18–19 (Part 1 of 3)**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾

These people forgot their souls not in every respect, but in the respect through which their welfare, perfection and happiness are attained. They did not forget them in the respect through which lies their appetite, their share and their desires. So He caused them to forget the welfare of their souls, such that they neither performed nor sought it, and to forget their faults and deficiencies, such that they neither removed nor avoided them. And He caused them to forget the perfection for which their souls were created, so they neither knew it nor sought it. Thus they are ignorant of the realities of their own souls from this standpoint, even though they know them from other standpoints.

(Benefit)

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾

He punished them for their forgetting Him by causing them to forget themselves. So they forgot the welfare of their souls, that they should perform it, and their faults, that they should correct them, and their shares, that they should take them. Among the greatest of the welfare of the soul and the most beneficial of its shares is its remembrance of its Lord and Originator. It has no bliss, no joy, no success and no righteousness except through remembering Him, loving Him, obeying Him, turning towards Him and turning away from all else. So He caused them to forget that, because they had forgotten Him, and this forgetting produced in them another forgetting. This is the opposite of the state of those who remembered Him and did not forget. Their remembrance of Him made them mindful of the welfare of their souls, so they performed it. It made them aware of their faults, so they corrected them. It made them recognise their lofty shares, so they hastened towards them. Thus He recompensed those (who remembered Him) for their remembrance by causing them to remember faith, its love, its remembrance and its gratitude. When their hearts were emptied of that, they found no escape from its opposite.

This shows you the perfection of His justice, may He be glorified, in decreeing disbelief and sins upon them. If His decree upon them of disbelief and sins is justice from Him towards them, then His decree of punishment upon them is more just and even more just. He, may He be glorified, executes His judgement upon His servant, and His judgement in it is just.

He has in this two decrees: the decree of the cause and the decree of the effect. Both are just. When the servant abandoned His remembrance and abandoned doing what He loves, He punished him by causing him to forget himself. This forgetting brought about in him the commission of what He hates and what displeases Him, by His decree which is just. So there followed for him, because of this doing and abandoning, punishments and pains from which he had no escape. Rather, they follow upon it as effects follow their causes. So this is pure justice from the Lord, may He be exalted. He is just towards the servant at the beginning and at the end. He is good in His justice, beloved in it and praised for it, and whoever is treated justly by Him, willingly or unwillingly, praises Him for it.

Al-Hasan said: "They entered the Fire, and yet His praise was in their hearts, though they found no way to it."

(Benefit)

The saying of Allah, the Exalted, indicates the obligation of self-examination: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow.﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]

He, may He be exalted, says: Let each one of you look at what he has sent forward for the Day of Resurrection of deeds: are they of the righteous deeds that will save him, or of the evil deeds that will destroy him?

Qatadah said: "Your Lord has never ceased to bring the Hour near until He made it like tomorrow."

The point is that the soul's righteousness comes through self-examination, and its corruption comes through neglecting it and drifting along with it.

(Benefit)

As for the acknowledgement of the Creator, it is a necessary, innate knowledge for the human being. No one is so heedless of it that he does not know it. Rather, he must have known it, even if it is supposed that he has forgotten it. For this reason, informing a person of it is called "reminding" (tadhkir), since it is a reminder of innate, necessary knowledge. The servant may forget it, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

In the authentic hadith: "Allah says to the disbeliever: 'Today I forget you as you forgot Me.'"

(Section)

Here is a matter that must be noticed: the Lord, may He be exalted, testified to the truth of what He reported. He is the most truthful of the truthful. He swore an oath upon it, and He is the most sincere of those who swear. He confirmed it by comparing it to what is actual, which admits no doubt in any way. He established upon it such evidences, both visible and demonstrative, that He made it witnessed and seen through insight, even if it is not seen with the eyes. Yet most souls are heedless of it. They do not prepare for it and do not take up its readiness. Those who prepare for it and take up its readiness are only single individuals here and there. Most of creation does not reflect on the purpose of their being brought into being and sent out into this abode. They do not reflect on the brevity of their stay in the house of delusion, nor on their departure and transfer from it, nor where they will journey and where they will settle. Sense has taken possession of them, the share of intellect in them is small, heedlessness has overwhelmed them, and the wishes that are like a mirage have deceived them, and long hope has tricked them. It is as if the one who remains will never depart, and as if one of them will never be resurrected or questioned. It is as if with every resident there is a decree from Allah to so-and-so son of so-and-so, granting him security from His punishment and success in His abundant reward.

As for sensual pleasures and soul-appetites, however they are obtained and from whatever direction they appear, they take hold of them, heedless of being called to account, secure from the consequence. They strive for what they can attain and leave what they are responsible for. They build up what they are about to leave, and ruin what they are about to arrive at. They are heedless of the Hereafter. The desires of their souls have distracted them, so they do not look at its welfare, nor do they set about gathering its provision for its journey. ﴿They forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

How utterly strange is the heedlessness of one whose moments are counted and whose breaths are numbered, while the mounts of night and day hasten him along, and yet he does not reflect where he is being carried or to what station he is being conveyed:

How can the eye sleep while it is at ease, when it does not know in which of the two abodes it will descend?

When death comes upon one of them, he is anxious about the ruin of his self and the loss of his pleasures, not about his past offences, nor about the evil of his final destination after death. If a thought of that occurs to one of them, he relies upon pardon or mercy, and he is certain that this is his lot, without doubt. If the intelligent person had summoned his mind, and what his intellect had summoned, and had journeyed with his thought, looked intently, and reflected upon the signs to understand the purpose of his creation, then the eye of the one who is departing would have looked at the road, the traveller would have taken provision, the sick would have sought treatment, and the prudent would have prepared for what may come.

So what is the assumption about a matter that is certain, as surely as the truthfulness of his faith and the strength of their certainty? It is as if they are witnessing the matter. The abodes of faith have become empty of their people, and its landmarks lie in ruin upon their foundations.

Ibn Wahb said: Muslim ibn Ali informed me, from al-Awza'i, who said:
"When the dawn broke, or before it, the early generations were as if birds were perched upon their heads, turning towards themselves. If a beloved of one of them had been absent for a while and then returned, he would not turn to him. They continued in this state until sunrise. Then some of them would rise and go to others, and they would begin with what most needed their attention concerning the affair of their return and what they were heading towards. Then they would turn to jurisprudence."

(Section)

Know that constant remembrance of the Lord, blessed and exalted, necessitates security from forgetting Him, which is the cause of the servant's wretchedness in his livelihood and in his return. For the forgetting of the Lord, may He be glorified and exalted, necessitates the forgetting of one's own self and its welfare. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

When the servant forgets himself, he turns away from its welfare, forgets it, and busies himself away from it, so it perishes and is corrupted, without doubt. Like one who has a crop, a garden or livestock, or something else whose welfare and success depend on his tending and caring for it, but he neglects it, forgets it and busies himself with other things, and so loses its welfare. It will certainly be corrupted.

This is the case even though another can take his place in caring for it. So what is the assumption about the corruption, destruction and wretchedness of one's own self, when he neglects and forgets it, busies himself away from its welfare, disables its care, and abandons the tending that would set it right? Whatever corruption, destruction, failure and deprivation you wish for, it will come.

This is the one whose whole affair has become neglected: his affair has slipped from his hands, his welfare has been lost, and the causes of ruin, failure and destruction surround him.

There is no way to be secure from that except by constant remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, and by keeping it always upon the tongue, so that the tongue never ceases to be moist with it. And that He be placed in the position of the servant's life, upon which he cannot do without. And in the position of his food, which if he lacks it, his body is corrupted and perishes. And in the position of water in severe thirst, and in the position of clothing in heat and cold, and in the position of shelter in the severity of winter and the scorching wind.

It is fitting for the servant to give the remembrance of Allah this position and even greater. For where is the ruin and corruption of the spirit and the heart compared to the ruin and corruption of the body?

That bodily ruin is unavoidable, and it may be followed by a righteousness that is also unavoidable. But the ruin of the heart and spirit is a ruin after which no righteousness or success is hoped for. There is no power and no strength except with Allah, the Most High, the Mighty.

[Section: Sins cause one to forget Allah]

Among their punishments is that they call for Allah's forgetting of His servant, leaving him, abandoning him, and leaving him between himself and his devil. There is the ruin after which no salvation is hoped for. Allah said: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do. And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hashr: 18–19]

So He commanded them to be mindful of Him, and forbade His believing servants from resembling those who forgot Him by abandoning His mindfulness. He informed them that He punishes whoever abandons mindfulness by causing him to forget himself, that is, causing him to forget its welfare, what saves it from His punishment, what brings it eternal life, and the perfection of its delight, joy and bliss. So Allah causes him to forget all of that, as recompense for his forgetting of His greatness, His fear, and attending to His command. You see the disobedient neglecting his soul's welfare and wasting it. Allah has made his heart heedless of His remembrance, and he has followed his desire, and his affair has become neglected. The welfare of his worldly life and his Hereafter has slipped from him. He has squandered his eternal happiness and exchanged it for the lowest of pleasures, which are only a summer cloud or the fancy of a phantom, as it has been said:

Dreams of sleep, or like a passing shadow; the intelligent person is not deceived by the like of them.

The greatest of punishments is the servant's forgetting of his own self, his neglecting of it, and his squandering of its portion and share from Allah. He sells that for deception, humiliation, and the most meagre price. He wastes the One without whom he has no sufficiency, and for whom there is no substitute, and he exchanges Him for one from whom comes all sufficiency, or from whom comes every substitute:

Whatever you lose of anything, it has a substitute; but there is no substitute for what you lose of Allah.

So Allah, may He be glorified, substitutes for everything else, and nothing can substitute for Him. He suffices in place of everything, and nothing suffices in His place. He grants protection from everything, and nothing grants protection from Him. He withholds from everything, and nothing withholds from Him. How can the servant be independent of obedience to one whose state is such, even for the blink of an eye?

How can he forget His remembrance and waste His command, until He causes him to forget himself, so that he loses it and wrongs it with the greatest wrong?

The servant did not wrong his Lord, but he wronged himself; and his Lord did not wrong him, but it is he who wronged himself.

[Section: Disobedience causes the servant to forget himself]

Among its punishments is that it causes the servant to forget himself. When he forgets himself, he neglects it, corrupts it and destroys it. If it is asked: How can the servant forget himself? And if he forgets himself, what does he remember? What is the meaning of his forgetting himself?

It is said: Yes, he forgets himself with the greatest forgetting. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

When they forgot their Lord, may He be glorified, He forgot them and caused them to forget themselves, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿They forgot Allah, so He forgot them.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 67]

So He, may He be glorified, punished whoever forgot Him with two punishments:

The first: that He forgot him.
The second: that He caused him to forget himself.

His forgetting of the servant, may He be glorified, means His neglect, His abandonment, His leaving him, and His squandering of him. Then ruin is nearer to him than the hand is to the mouth. As for His causing him to forget himself, it means that He causes him to forget its lofty shares, the causes of its happiness, its success and its righteousness, and what it is perfected by. By forgetting all of that, it does not come to his mind, he does not make it the object of his remembrance, and he does not direct his resolve towards it so as to desire it. For it does not pass through his mind until he intends it and prefers it.

Furthermore, He causes him to forget the faults, deficiencies and afflictions of his soul, so the thought of removing them does not occur to him.

Furthermore, He causes him to forget the diseases of his soul and heart and their pains, so the thought of treating them does not occur to his heart, nor the effort to remove their ailments and diseases, which lead to corruption and ruin. He is sick, overwhelmed by the disease, and his disease is moving towards destruction, yet he is not aware of his sickness, and the thought of treating it does not occur to his mind. This is among the greatest of punishments, both general and particular.

What punishment could be greater than that of one who neglects and wastes his soul, forgets its welfare, its disease and its remedy, and the causes of its happiness, success, righteousness and eternal life in enduring bliss? Whoever reflects on this point will see clearly that most of these people have forgotten the reality of their souls, wasted them, and squandered their share from Allah. They have sold them cheaply for a meagre price, in a sale of deception. This will only become apparent to them at death, and it will become fully apparent on the Day of Mutual Deception (Yawm al-Taghabun), the day when the servant will realise that he was deceived in the contract he made for his soul in this abode, and in the trade in which he traded for his return. For everyone trades in this world for his Hereafter.

Those who lose, who think that they are the people of profit and gain, have bought the life of this world, with their share and their pleasures in it, at the price of the Hereafter and their share in it. So they have squandered their good things in their worldly life and enjoyed them, and were content with them and at rest with them. Their striving was for obtaining them. So they sold, bought and traded, and they exchanged the deferred for the immediate, credit for cash, and the absent for the present. They said: "This is prudence." One of them says:

Take what you see, and leave what you have only heard of.

How then should I sell a present, cash, witnessed thing in this abode for an absent thing on credit in another abode other than this one? To this is added the weakness of faith, the strength of the call of desire, love of the immediate, and imitating the sons of the same kind. Most of creation is in this losing trade, concerning which Allah said about its people: ﴿Those are the ones who have bought the life of this world at the price of the Hereafter, so the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be helped.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 86]

And He said about them: ﴿So their trade did not profit them, nor were they guided.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 16]

So when the Day of Mutual Deception comes, the loss in this trade will become apparent to them, and souls will be torn apart by regret over them.

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 59, verses 18–19 (part 2 of 3):

As for the winners, they sold the perishable for the everlasting, the base for the precious, and the trivial for the magnificent. They said: "What is the worth of this world, from its beginning to its end, that we should sell our share of Allah the Exalted and the Last Abode for it? How can a servant obtain from it in this short time, which in reality is like the nap of a dream, and which has no relation whatsoever to the Abode of Permanence?" Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And the day He gathers them, [it will be] as if they had not remained but an hour of [one] day, knowing each other [in recognition] among themselves﴾ [Yunus: 45].

Allah the Exalted also says: ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when is its arrival? In what [position] are you to mention it? To your Lord is its finality. You are only a warner for those who fear it. It will be, on the day they see it, as if they had not remained but an evening or its morning﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 42–46].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day. [This is] notification﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 35].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He will say, "How long did you remain on earth in number of years?" They will say, "We remained a day or part of a day; so ask those who keep count." He will say, "You remained not but a little, if you had only known"﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 112–114].

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿The day the Horn is blown, and We gather the criminals that day, blue-eyed, whispering among themselves, "You remained not but ten [days]." We are most knowing of what they say when they of best course will say, "You remained not but a day"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 102–104].

This, then, is the reality of the world when the Day of Resurrection arrives. When they knew how brief their stay in it had been, and that for them there is another abode besides this abode, namely the abode of life and the abode of permanence, they saw that selling the abode of permanence for the abode of perishing is among the greatest deceptions. So they traded the trade of the discerning, and were not deceived by the trade of the foolish among people. Thus, on the Day of Mutual Deception, the profit of their trade and the value of what they had bought became manifest to them. Every person in this world is a seller, a buyer and a trader, and every person goes forth in the morning, selling his soul; either he frees it or he destroys it.

﴿Indeed, Allah has purchased from the believers their lives and their wealth in exchange for that they will have Paradise. They fight in the cause of Allah, so they kill and are killed. A true promise [binding] upon Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. And who is truer to his covenant than Allah? So rejoice in your transaction which you have contracted. And that is the great attainment﴾ [al-Tawbah: 111].

This is the first installment of the price of this trade. So trade, O bankrupt ones, and you who cannot afford this price: here is another price. If you are of the people of this trade, then give this price: ﴿The repentant, the worshippers, the praisers, the travelers, the bowers, the prostrators, those who enjoin what is good and forbid what is wrong, and those who observe the limits of Allah. And give good tidings to the believers﴾ [al-Tawbah: 112].

﴿O you who have believed, shall I guide you to a transaction that will save you from a painful punishment? [It is that] you believe in Allah and His Messenger and strive in the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is best for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Saff: 10–11].

The point is that sins make the servant forget his share of this profitable trade and occupy him with the losing trade, and that alone is sufficient as a punishment. And Allah is the One sought for help.

[Section: The Station of Self-Accounting]
[From the station of self-accounting, the station of repentance becomes valid for him]

Section: The Station of Self-Accounting

Let us return to the mention of the stations of "﴿You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help﴾", which a servant does not belong to until he descends into its stations.

We have mentioned from among them alertness, insight, reflection and resolve.

These four stations are, for all the other stations, like a foundation for a building, and upon them depend the stations of the journey to Allah. The journey to Him cannot be conceived without descending into them at all. They follow the order of physical travel: the one who resides in his homeland cannot undertake a journey until he awakens from his heedlessness regarding the journey; then he gains insight into the matter of his journey and its danger, and what benefit and advantage it holds for him; then he reflects on the preparations for the journey, the provisions, and the readying of its equipment; then he resolves upon it. When he has resolved and gathered his intention, he moves to the station of self-accounting, which is distinguishing between what is his and what is owed by him. So he keeps what is his and discharges what he owes, because he is a traveler on a journey from which none returns.

From the station of self-accounting, the station of repentance becomes valid for him, because when he takes account of himself, he recognizes what right is upon him, so he leaves it and is absolved of it before its owner. This is the reality of repentance, so placing self-accounting before it is more appropriate.

There is also a reason for placing repentance before it: self-accounting is not valid except after repentance is sound.

The truth is that repentance lies between two self-accountings: a self-accounting before it, which requires it, and a self-accounting after it, which requires its preservation. Repentance is thus framed by two self-accountings. Allah's saying indicates self-accounting: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾ [al-Hashr: 18]. So Allah the Glorified commanded the servant to look at what he has sent forward for tomorrow, and this includes taking account of himself regarding it and looking into whether what he has sent forward is fit for him to meet Allah with, or is not fit.

The purpose of this looking is what it necessitates and requires of complete preparation for the Day of Return, and the sending forward of what saves him from the punishment of Allah and whitens his face before Allah. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Take account of yourselves before you are taken to account, weigh yourselves before you are weighed, and adorn yourselves for the Great Exposure: ﴿On that Day you will be exhibited; not a secret of yours will be concealed﴾ [al-Haqqah: 18]," or he said: "before the One to whom your deeds are not hidden."

[Pillars of Self-Accounting]
[The First Pillar: Comparison between what belongs to the servant and what belongs to Allah]

The author of the Manazil said: Self-accounting has three pillars.

The first of them: that you compare between His blessing and your offence.

That is, you compare what is from Allah and what is from you. Then the disparity becomes evident to you, and you know that there is nothing but His pardon and His mercy, or else destruction and ruin.

Through this comparison you know that the Lord is Lord and the servant is servant, the reality of the self and its attributes becomes clear to you, along with the greatness of the majesty of Lordship, and the Lord's uniqueness in perfection and bounty, and that every blessing from Him is a favour and every affliction from Him is justice. Before this comparison you were ignorant of the reality of your self and of the lordship of its Originator and Creator. When you compare, it becomes apparent to you that the self is the source of every evil and the foundation of every deficiency, that its limit is ignorance and wrongdoing, and that were it not for Allah's favour and mercy in purifying it, it would never have been purified; and were it not for His guidance, it would never have been guided; and were it not for His direction and success, it would never have reached any good at all. The attainment of that by the self comes from its Creator and Originator, and its dependence upon Him is like the dependence of its existence upon His bringing it into being. Just as the self has no existence from itself, so it has no perfection of existence from itself; it has nothing from itself but non-existence: non-existence of essence and non-existence of perfection. At that point you truly say: "I acknowledge Your blessing upon me, and I acknowledge my sin."

Then you compare between the good deeds and the bad deeds, and through this comparison you know which of the two is greater and weightier in quantity and quality.

This second comparison is a comparison between your actions and what is solely from yourself.

He said: This comparison is difficult for one who lacks three things: the light of wisdom, a low opinion of the self, and the ability to distinguish blessing from trial.

That is, this comparison and self-accounting depend upon the light of wisdom, which is the light with which Allah illuminated the hearts of the followers of the Messengers. By its measure you perceive the disparity and become able to take account.

The light of wisdom here is the knowledge by which the servant distinguishes between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, the harmful and the beneficial, the complete and the deficient, good and evil, and by which he perceives the ranks of deeds, the preferred and the disfavoured, the accepted and the rejected. The more his share of this light, the more complete and perfect his share of self-accounting.

As for a low opinion of the self, one needs it because a good opinion of the self prevents thorough scrutiny and confuses him, so he sees faults as virtues and defects as perfections, for the one who loves sees the faults of his beloved in the same way.

"The eye of contentment is blind to every flaw, just as the eye of anger reveals all the faults."

None thinks ill of himself except one who knows himself, and whoever thinks well of himself is among the most ignorant of people about himself.

As for distinguishing blessing from trial: he must differentiate between the blessing through which kindness and gentleness are seen, and through which he is assisted in attaining his eternal happiness, and the blessing through which gradual enticement is seen. How many are led on gradually by blessings while unaware, enchanted by the praise of the ignorant, deceived by Allah's granting of his needs and His concealing of him! Most of creation think that these three are signs of happiness and success; that is the extent of their knowledge.

When these three are complete in him, he then knows that whatever blessings of Allah upon him are gathered toward Allah are a true blessing, and whatever He has separated from him and taken from him is trial in the form of blessing and affliction in the form of gift. So let him beware, for he is being led on gradually. He should also distinguish between favour and proof, for how often one of them is confused for the other! The servant is between a favour from Allah upon him and a proof from Him against him, and he is never free of both. The religious command contains both His favour and His proof. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Allah has certainly conferred favour upon the believers when He sent among them a Messenger from themselves﴾ [Al 'Imran: 164]. He says: ﴿Rather, Allah confers favour upon you that He has guided you to faith﴾ [al-Hujurat: 17]. He says: ﴿So to Allah belongs the conclusive argument﴾ [al-An'am: 149].

The cosmic command also contains His favour and His proof. When He decrees for him, in the cosmic sense, a decree accompanied by the connection of the religious command to it, it is a favour upon him; and if it is not accompanied by the religious command, it is a proof against him.

Likewise, His religious command, when connected to His cosmic decree, his being granted the ability to fulfil it is a favour from Him upon him; and if it is stripped of His cosmic decree, it becomes a proof against him. Favour lies in the conjunction of one of the two commands with the other, and proof lies in the separation of one from the other. Thus every knowledge accompanied by a deed that pleases Allah the Glorified is a favour, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every power, outward and inward, accompanied by the execution of His pleasure and commands is a favour, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every state accompanied by an effect in supporting His religion and calling to it is a favour from Him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every wealth joined with spending in the way of Allah and in obedience to Him, seeking neither reward nor thanks, is a favour from Allah upon him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every free time joined with occupation in what the Lord desires from His servant is a favour upon him, and otherwise it is a proof.

Every acceptance among people, and every honour and love directed toward him, when connected with humility before the Lord, lowliness and brokenness, awareness of the defect of the self and of one's deeds, and offering sincere advice to creation, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every insight and admonition, reminder and instruction from the Truth, the Glorified, to the servant, when connected with lessons, an increase in reason, and knowledge in faith, is a favour; otherwise it is a proof.

Every state with Allah the Exalted, or station connected with journeying to Allah and preferring His desire over the servant's desire, is a favour from Allah. But if it is accompanied by halting at it and contentment with it, and preferring its requirement out of the pleasure of the self in it, its calm in it and its inclination toward it, it is a proof from Allah against him.

So let the servant contemplate this most momentous place, and distinguish between the positions of favours and trials, and proofs and blessings. How often does this become confused for the elite of people and the practitioners of the spiritual path! And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.

[Section: The Second Pillar: Distinguishing between what is for the servant and what is upon him]

Section

The second pillar of the pillars of self-accounting is: that you distinguish what is due to the Truth upon you, and between what is yours and what is upon you, of the obligations of servitude, the commitment to obedience, and the avoidance of

...disobedience, and between what is yours and what is upon you. What is yours is the lawfully permissible (mubah shar'i). Upon you is a right, and you have a right. So fulfil what is upon you, and it will give you what is yours.

It is necessary to distinguish between what is yours and what is upon you, and to give every person with a right his right.

Many people treat much of what is their duty as falling under what is optional for them. They therefore hesitate between doing and not doing it, and if they do it, they regard it as a supererogatory favour they have performed, not a right they have discharged.

Opposite these are those who regard much of what is optional for them to do or leave as falling under what is their duty to do or leave. So they worship God by abandoning what is permitted to them to do, as in abandoning many lawful things, and they think this is obligatory upon them. Or they worship God by doing what is permitted to them to leave, and they think this is obligatory upon them.

An example of the first kind is someone who worships God by abstaining from marriage, or from eating meat, or fruit, for example, or from good foods and clothing. Out of ignorance, he regards this as something required of him, so he makes it obligatory upon himself to abstain, or he considers abstaining from it to be among the best acts of drawing near to God and the most excellent acts of obedience. The Prophet ﷺ rejected this view held by some people. In the Sahih it is reported that a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ asked about his worship in private, and they seemed to belittle it. One of them said: "As for me, I will not eat meat." Another said: "As for me, I will not marry women." Another said: "As for me, I will not sleep on a bed." When the Prophet ﷺ heard of their statement, he delivered a sermon and said: "What is the matter with people who say, 'As for me, I will not eat meat,' and another says, 'As for me, I will not marry,' and another says, 'As for me, I will not sleep on a bed'? But I marry women, I eat meat, I sleep and I pray at night, I fast and I break my fast. Whoever turns away from my Sunnah (way), he is not of me." So he disassociated himself from those who turned away from his Sunnah, and they worshipped God by abandoning what He had permitted His servants of good things, out of aversion to it, believing that aversion to it and forsaking it is worship. This person did not distinguish between what is upon him and what is his.

An example of the second kind is someone who worships God through innovated acts of worship (bid'ah, innovation in religion), which he believes bring about spiritual states, unveiling, and the power to influence. These matters have necessary consequences that cannot occur at all without them. So he commits himself to observing those consequences by doing or abstaining, and he regards them as a right owed to God upon him, while in fact they are a right for him, and he may leave them. This is like the spiritual exercises and the practices that many wayfarers have laid down according to their own tastes, ecstasies, and terminologies, without distinguishing between what in them is the servant's own portion and what is the right God has upon him. This is one kind, and that is another kind.

[Section: The Third Pillar: Being Pleased with Obedience and Reproaching Oneself for Disobedience]

Among the pillars of self-accounting is what the author of al-Manazil (Abu Isma'il al-Harawi) mentioned. He said:

"The third: that you know that every act of obedience you are pleased with from yourself is against you, and every sin for which you reproach your brother is against you (lit. 'comes to you')."

A servant's being pleased with his obedience is a sign of his good opinion of himself, his ignorance of the rights of servanthood, and his failure to act in the way that the Lord, may His majesty be exalted, deserves and that it is fitting to treat Him.

The sum of this is that his ignorance of himself, its attributes, its afflictions, and the defects of his deeds, along with his ignorance of his Lord, His rights, and what He deserves to be treated with, gives rise to his being pleased with his obedience and having a good opinion of it. From this arise vanity, arrogance, and afflictions greater than the major visible sins such as adultery, drinking wine, fleeing from battle, and the like.

So being pleased with obedience is among the follies and foolishness of the soul.

Those of resolve and insight are the most diligent in seeking forgiveness after acts of obedience, because they witness their own shortcomings in them, and their failure to stand before God in them as befits His majesty and greatness. They know that had it not been for the command, none of them would have undertaken such worship, nor would God have been pleased with it for His Master.

God Most High commanded His delegation and the pilgrims to His House to seek His forgiveness after they depart from Arafat, which is the greatest and most excellent of the standing places. He said: ﴿So when you depart from Arafat, remember Allah at the Sacred Monument. And remember Him as He has guided you, although you were before it among those astray. Then depart from where the people depart and seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 198-199]

He Most High also said: ﴿And those who seek forgiveness before dawn.﴾ [Al-Imran: 17]

Al-Hasan said: "They extended the prayer until the pre-dawn, then they sat seeking forgiveness from Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

In the Sahih, it is reported that the Prophet ﷺ, when he finished the prayer, would seek forgiveness three times, then say: "O Allah, You are As-Salam (Peace), and from You is peace. Blessed are You, O Possessor of majesty and honour."

God Most High commanded him to seek forgiveness after fulfilling the message, after discharging what was upon him of its burdens, after performing the obligatory Hajj, and as his end drew near. He said at the end of a surah revealed to him: ﴿When the victory of Allah has come and the conquest, and you see the people entering into the religion of Allah in multitudes, then exalt with the praise of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.﴾ [An-Nasr: 1-3]

From here, Umar and Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, understood that this was the announcement of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ's death, which Allah had informed him of. So He commanded him to seek His forgiveness after completing what was upon him. It was as if it were a notification: "You have discharged what was upon you, and nothing remains upon you, so let your conclusion be seeking forgiveness," just as it was the conclusion of the prayer, the Hajj, and the night prayer. The conclusion of ablution as well is that one says after finishing: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. I bear witness that there is no deity except You. I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance. O Allah, make me of those who repent often, and make me of those who purify themselves."

This is the attitude of one who knows what is due to God and fitting to His majesty of the rights and conditions of servanthood, not the ignorance of those who make claims and their wild utterances.

Some of the knowers of God said: "Whenever you are pleased with yourself and your deed for God's sake, know that He is not pleased with it. Whoever knows that his soul is the abode of every fault and evil, and that his deed is exposed to every blight and deficiency, how could he be pleased with his soul and his deed for God?"

How excellent is the statement of Shaykh Abu Madyan, when he says: "Whoever realises servanthood sees his actions with the eye of hypocrisy (riya'), his states with the eye of pretension, and his words with the eye of fabrication. Whenever the sought object becomes great in your heart, your self becomes small in your eyes, and the price you pay to obtain it becomes insignificant. Whenever you witness the reality of lordship and the reality of servanthood, and you know God and you know the self, and it becomes clear to you that the merchandise you have does not suit the True King, and even if you came with the deeds of both jinn and humankind you would fear their consequence, He accepts it only by His generosity, bounty, and grace, and He rewards you for it also by His generosity, bounty, and grace."

As for his saying: "Every sin for which you reproach your brother is against you (comes to you)," it may mean: that it will inevitably come to you and you will commit it. This is derived from the hadith that al-Tirmidhi reported in his Jami' from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever reproaches his brother for a sin, he will not die until he commits it."

Imam Ahmad said, explaining this hadith: "[That is] for a sin from which he has already repented."

Also, in reproaching there is a hidden kind of gloating over the one who is reproached.

In al-Tirmidhi also, it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "Do not display gloating toward your brother, lest Allah have mercy on him and test you."

It may also mean: that your reproaching your brother for his sin is greater in sinfulness than his sin, and worse than his disobedience, because it contains the boldness of obedience, the self-praise of the soul, the thanking of it, and proclaiming it free from sin while your brother has been afflicted by it. Perhaps his being broken by his sin, the humiliation and submission it produced in him, his belittling of himself, and his freeing himself from the disease of self-claim, pride, and self-admiration, and his standing before God with bowed head, lowered gaze, and broken heart, is more beneficial to him and better than the boldness of your obedience, your multiplying it and counting on it, and your taking favour with God and His creation because of it. How near this disobedient one is to the mercy of God, and how near this one who boasts is to God's wrath! A sin by which you are humbled before Him is more beloved to Him than an act of obedience by which you boast before Him. Your sleeping and waking up regretful is better than your spending the night standing in prayer and waking up self-admiring, for the self-admirer, his deed does not ascend. And your laughing while acknowledging your fault is better than your weeping while boasting. The moaning of sinners is more beloved to God than the chanting of the glorifiers who boast. Perhaps God gave him this sin as a remedy to draw out a deadly disease that is in you without your noticing.

God has secrets concerning those who obey Him and those who disobey Him that no one knows but Him, and only people of insight perceive them, so they know of them as much as human knowledge can attain. Beyond that is what the noble recording angels do not perceive. The Prophet ﷺ said: "If the slave-woman of one of you commits fornication, let him impose the prescribed punishment upon her and not reproach her (la yuthrib)." That is, he should not reproach her, from the words of Yusuf, peace be upon him, to his brothers: ﴿No reproach will there be upon you today.﴾ [Yusuf: 92] Indeed, the scale is in the hand of God, and the judgment belongs to God. So the whip with which this disobedient one is struck is in the hand of the Turner of hearts. The intent is to enforce the legal punishment, not to reproach or rebuke. No one feels secure from the turns of destiny and its assault except those ignorant of God. God Most High said to the most knowing of creation of Him and the closest of them to Him in means: ﴿And if We had not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined to them a little.﴾ [Al-Isra: 74] And Yusuf the truthful said: ﴿And unless You turn away from me their plot, I would incline toward them and be among the ignorant.﴾ [Yusuf: 33]

The common oath of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was: "No, by the Turner of hearts."

He also said: "There is no heart but that it is between two of the fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to make it firm, He makes it firm, and if He wills to make it swerve, He makes it swerve." Then he said: "O Allah, Turner of hearts, make our hearts firm upon Your religion. O Allah, Director of hearts, direct our hearts to Your obedience."

Commentary of Ibn al-Qayyim (al-Tafsir al-Qayyim) on surah 59, verse 21:

Al-Hafiz Abu Musa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ali, who said: "I guarantee that whoever recites these twenty verses, Allah the Exalted will protect him from every oppressive devil, every rebellious devil, every harmful beast, and every transgressing thief: the Ayat al-Kursi, three verses from al-A'raf, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth﴾, ten from al-Saffat, three verses from al-Rahman, ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind﴾, and the closing verses of Surat al-Hashr, ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of Allah﴾."

Muhammad ibn Aban said: While a man was praying in the mosque, he suddenly found something beside him, so he jumped away from it. It said: "Do not be harmed by me. I came to you for the sake of Allah the Exalted. Go to Urwah and ask him: What is it that he seeks refuge with?" He meant protection from Iblis and the Abalis (the many devils).

[Urwah] said: "Say: I believe in Allah, the Mighty, alone, and I disbelieve in the idols (jibt) and the tyrants (taghut), and I hold fast to the firmest handhold that has no breaking, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing."

"Sufficient for me is Allah, and He is the best disposer. Allah hears whoever calls upon Him. There is no end beyond Allah."

Bishr ibn Mansur narrated from Wuhayb ibn al-Ward, who said: A man went out to the graveyard an hour after nightfall. He said: "I heard a loud sound, or a voice, and a couch was brought and placed down, and something came and sat upon it."

He said: "His soldiers gathered around him. Then he shouted: 'Who will deal with Urwah ibn al-Zubayr for me?' No one answered him until the voices multiplied to whatever extent Allah willed. One of them said: 'I will deal with him.' He set off toward Medina, and I was watching. Then he soon returned and said: 'There is no way to reach Urwah. Woe to you! I found him saying words, in the morning and in the evening, and we cannot reach him with them.'"

The man said: "When morning came, I said to my family: 'Prepare me.' I came to Medina and asked about him until I was guided to him. There he was, an elderly man. I said: 'Tell me something you say in the morning and in the evening.' He refused to tell me, so I informed him of what I had seen and heard. He said: 'I do not know, except that I say in the morning: I believe in Allah, the Mighty, and I disbelieve in the idols and the tyrants, and I hold fast to the firmest handhold that has no breaking, and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.'"

[He said:] "When you reach the morning, say it three times, and when you reach the evening, say it three times."

Abu Musa mentioned from Muslim al-Battin, who said: Jibril said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed, an 'Ifrit from the jinn is plotting against you. When you retire to your bed, say: 'I seek refuge in the perfect words of Allah, which no righteous nor wicked person can transgress, from the evil of what descends from the sky and what ascends into it, and from the evil of what He created in the earth and what emerges from it, and from the evil of the trials of night and day, and from the evil of the visitors of night and day, except a visitor who comes with good, O Most Merciful.'"

It is established in the Sahih that the devil flees from the call to prayer (adhan). Sahl ibn Abi Salih said: My father sent me to the Banu Harithah, and with me was a boy or companion of ours. A caller called out to him from a garden wall by his name, and the one with me looked up at the wall but saw nothing. I mentioned that to my father, and he said: "Had I known you would encounter this, I would not have sent you. Rather, when you hear a voice, call out the prayer, for I heard Abu Hurayrah narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'Indeed, when the devil is called to prayer, he turns away while passing wind (hasis),'" and in another narration: "When he hears the call, he turns away while passing wind, until he does not hear the adhan," the hadith.

Al-Hafiz Abu Musa mentioned from the hadith of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

"Increase your recitation of 'There is no god but Allah' and seeking forgiveness, for the devil said: 'I have destroyed them with sins, and they have destroyed me with the statement "There is no god but Allah" and seeking forgiveness. When I saw that from them, I destroyed them with desires, until they think they are guided, so they do not seek forgiveness.'"

He also mentioned, from Ibrahim ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Ikrimah, who said: A traveler was passing by a sleeping man and saw devils around him. The traveler heard one of the devils say to his companion: "Go and corrupt this sleeper's heart." When it approached him, it returned to its companion and said: "He has slept upon a verse; we have no way to reach him." So it went to the sleeper, but when it drew near, it returned and said: "You are right," and it departed.

Then the traveler woke him and informed him of what he had seen of the devils. He said: "Tell me, upon which verse did you sleep?" He said: "Upon this verse: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days, then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, which it follows rapidly, and [He created] the sun and the moon and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ (7:54)."

Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim said: I used to see in my house ...

It was said: "O Abu al-Nadr, move away from our neighborhood."

He said: "This grieved me greatly, so I wrote to Kufa, to Ibn Idris, al-Muharibi, and Abu Usamah. Al-Muharibi wrote back to me: 'A well in Medina whose bucket-rope kept being cut. A caravan stopped there, and they complained of this to them. They called for a bucket of water, then spoke these words and poured it into the well, and fire came out of the well and was extinguished at the well's rim.'"

Abu al-Nadr said: "I took a pitcher of water, then spoke these words over it, then I went around the corners of the house and sprinkled it. They shouted at me: 'You have burned us! We will move away from you!' The words are: 'In the name of Allah. We have entered the evening by Allah, besides whom nothing can resist, and by the might of Allah which cannot be overcome or oppressed, and by the mighty authority of Allah we take shelter, and by all His Most Beautiful Names I seek refuge from the Abalis, and from the evil of the devils of mankind and jinn, and from the evil of whoever is open or secret, and from the evil of what goes out by night and hides by day, and what hides by night and goes out by day, and from the evil of what He created, multiplied and originated, and from the evil of Iblis and his armies, and from the evil of every creature whose forelock You hold. Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path.'
